jobs.title: Account Executive, MSP
jobs.description_html:
Get to Know Us

Horizon3 is a fast-growing, remote cybersecurity company dedicated to enabling organizations to proactively find, fix, and verify exploitable attack vectors before criminals exploit them. Our flagship NodeZero™ platform delivers production-safe autonomous pentests and other key assessment operations that scale across the largest internal, external, cloud, and hybrid cloud environments.

NodeZero has been adopted by organizations of all sizes, from small educational institutions to government agencies and Global 100 enterprises. It is used by ITOps and SecOps teams, consulting pentesters, and MSSPs and MSPs.

We are a team of former U.S. Special Operations cyber operators, startup engineers and operators, and formerly frustrated cybersecurity practitioners. We are committed to solving persistent security challenges, including ineffective tools, false positives, alert fatigue, blind spots, checkbox security culture, cybersecurity skills shortages, and the cost and delay of traditional consulting. We are learn-it-alls who value respect, collaboration, ownership, and results.

The Opportunity

Horizon3 is seeking an experienced Account Executive to accelerate revenue growth and NodeZero adoption through Managed Service Providers (MSPs) and the Pax8 Marketplace.

In this role, you will own the full sales cycle—from identifying and recruiting high-potential MSP partners to leading discovery, building compelling business cases, negotiating agreements, and closing business. You will engage MSP owners, executives, and technical leaders to connect NodeZero's capabilities to their business priorities, customer needs, and opportunities to build differentiated, profitable security services.

Working closely with the Pax8 sales organization and Horizon3's internal teams, you will turn inbound interest and targeted outbound prospecting into a predictable pipeline of qualified opportunities. The ideal candidate brings sound commercial judgment, technical credibility, disciplined execution, and the ability to independently move opportunities forward in a fast-paced environment.

What You’ll Do

  • Own revenue growth through the Pax8 MSP motion, consistently delivering against sales quotas and revenue and profitability goals.

  • Develop and execute targeted outbound prospecting strategies to engage prospective Pax8 MSP partners and build a consistent pipeline of new business.

  • Lead consultative discovery with MSP owners, executives, and technical leaders to understand their security offerings, operating models, customer requirements, and growth priorities.

  • Articulate a compelling business case for NodeZero, connecting technical capabilities to differentiated services, operational efficiency, recurring revenue opportunities, and measurable customer value.

  • Build productive relationships with the Pax8 sales organization to coordinate account engagement, advance joint opportunities, and accelerate new MSP partner acquisition and adoption.

  • Deliver tailored presentations, demonstrations, and proposals, partnering with technical resources as needed to address requirements, resolve objections, and build buying confidence.

  • Negotiate commercial terms and close business with a clear understanding of partner economics, stakeholder priorities, and the purchasing process.

  • Partner with Marketing to support events and campaigns that build MSP awareness and translate engagement into qualified opportunities and revenue.

  • Collaborate with Engineering and Marketing to communicate partner feedback and coordinate resolution of product-related concerns, including quality, delivery, and design requirements.

  • Maintain accurate forecasts and detailed sales tracking, with clear visibility into opportunity qualification, decision-makers, next steps, risks, and expected close dates.

  • Sustain disciplined prospecting and follow-through, building sufficient pipeline coverage to achieve quarterly goals and adjusting priorities based on conversion rates and business impact.

What You’ll Bring

  • 3–5+ years of successful B2B technology sales experience, with a demonstrated track record selling cybersecurity solutions.

  • Proven experience selling to or through MSPs, with an understanding of how they evaluate technology, build service offerings, and generate recurring revenue.

  • A consistent record of meeting or exceeding quota and independently managing opportunities from initial engagement through negotiation and close.

  • Strong command of consultative, solution-selling, or target-account-selling techniques, including discovery, qualification, stakeholder alignment, and business-case development.

  • The ability to translate complex networking and security challenges into clear business value for both technical and executive audiences.

  • Strong presentation skills and the ability to communicate technical solutions and business concepts through tailored demonstrations and proposals.

  • Sound commercial judgment and a successful track record navigating objections, negotiating agreements, and closing multi-stakeholder opportunities.

  • Disciplined pipeline management, forecasting, account planning, and sales execution, with clear ownership of commitments and results.

  • Comfort working in a fast-paced startup environment, with a hands-on approach, adaptability, and a positive, solutions-focused mindset.

We are a fully remote company. This role may require up to 20% travel to support partner engagements, events, and business development activities.

At Horizon3, we believe that our people are our greatest asset, and our compensation philosophy reflects this core value. jobs.title: Applied AI Engineer, Autonomous Defense
jobs.description_html:
Get to Know Us

Horizon3 is a fast-growing, remote cybersecurity company dedicated to the mission of enabling organizations to proactively find and fix and verify exploitable attack vectors before criminals exploit them. Our flagship product, the NodeZeroTM platform, delivers production-safe autonomous pentests and other key assessment operations that scale across the largest internal, external, cloud, and hybrid cloud environments. NodeZero has been adopted by organizations of all sizes, from small educational institutions to government agencies and Global 100 enterprises. It is used by ITOps/SecOps teams, consulting pentesters, and MSSPs and MSPs. 

We are a fusion of former U.S. Special Operations cyber operators, startup engineers, and formerly frustrated cybersecurity practitioners. We're committed to helping solve our common security problems: ineffective security tools, false positives resulting in alert fatigue, blind spots, "checkbox” security culture, cybersecurity skills shortage, and the long lead time and expense of hiring outside consultants. Collectively, we are a team of learn it alls, committed to a culture of respect, collaboration, ownership, and results.

 

What You'll Do

We're looking for an AI Researcher to build the agents that turn our offensive knowledge into defensive action.

You'll build agents that reason from a proven attack path to the specific control changes that break it - EDR policy, firewall and segmentation rules, conditional access, detection content, cloud IAM, GPO - apply or stage those changes in the customer's environment, and then prove the fix by re-running the attack.

That last part is why this is tractable. Most defensive AI has no ground truth and gets graded on whether its advice sounds reasonable. Ours gets graded on whether the attack still works. You will have a real outcome signal on a short loop, and hundreds of thousands of prior tests to learn from. It is also why this is hard. These agents run inside customer tenants and modify production security controls. A bad change is an outage or a new hole in someone's defense. The reasoning problem and the safety problem are the same problem here, and you will own both.

The goal is closed-loop defense: find, fix, verify, running autonomously at enterprise scale. If you want to work on agents where the feedback is real and the stakes are real, this is the job for you.

Responsibilities

  • Build the reasoning systems that map proven attack paths and exploitation telemetry to specific, applicable control changes, ranked by effectiveness against operational blast radius.

  • Turn our pentest data into training and evaluation data. Extract the signal of why an attack succeeded in one environment and failed in another.

  • Design and run counterfactual experiments in representative test environments: would this change have broken this attack chain, what does it cost operationally, and does it generalize beyond the tenant it was learned in.

  • Design the reasoning layer over heterogeneous control planes so an agent can work across vendor APIs with different policy models without a hardcoded playbook per product.

  • Design the safety architecture for autonomous change — dry-run and simulation, blast-radius classification, approval gates for high-impact actions, staged rollout, rollback, and an audit trail a customer's change board will accept.

  • Work with our attack engineers and detection engineers to define target agent behavior and diagnose failure modes: ineffective remediations, over-broad changes, business-breaking policy edits, and recommendations that look right and don't hold on re-test.

  • Own problems end to end in a 0→1 environment where requirements are ambiguous, systems move fast, and reliability matters, because the output lands in someone's production security posture.

What You'll Bring

Required

  • Strong ML engineering experience building, evaluating, and deploying production AI systems, with hands-on work in deep learning, transformer models, and PyTorch.

  • Hands-on experience with at least one of: post-training large language models (supervised fine-tuning, distillation, preference optimization, RL), or designing agentic systems with tool use, planning, and long-horizon execution that hold up outside a demo.

  • A track record of building evaluation systems for open-ended tasks where there is no clean label and success is judged by outcome.

  • Experience reasoning over structured, heterogeneous, messy real-world data — configurations, graphs, logs, policy documents — rather than clean benchmark datasets.

  • Strong software engineering fundamentals and a track record of shipping and maintaining production-quality code in Python, not just scripts and proofs of concept.

  • Experience with data pipelines, distributed systems, and cloud infrastructure, preferably AWS.

  • Ability to work across model behavior, APIs, and infrastructure, and to collaborate closely with attack engineers, detection engineers, product, and infrastructure.

  • Ability to independently research unfamiliar systems and rapidly become the team's expert.

  • Strong written and verbal communication, including clear technical documentation.

  • Master's in Computer Science, Machine Learning, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience, plus 4+ years of professional engineering experience.

You do not need to have been a pentester or a SOC analyst. You do need to be seriously interested in how attackers and defenders actually operate, and willing to learn it in depth. The reasoning we are building cannot be designed by someone who does not understand the domain.

Preferred

  • Background in detection engineering, purple teaming, security engineering, offensive security, or incident response.

  • Hands-on familiarity with security control planes and their APIs and policy models: EDR (CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Defender), firewalls and segmentation (Palo Alto, Fortinet), identity and conditional access (Entra ID, Okta), SIEM and detection content (Splunk, Sentinel), cloud IAM, WAF, MDM, and GPO.

  • Experience with causal or counterfactual inference, or with graph reasoning, planning, and search over large state spaces. Familiarity with Neo4j and attack-path analysis.

  • Experience building automation that takes write actions in production systems, along with the safety and change-management machinery around it.

  • Experience with adversarial robustness or prompt injection, particularly where an agent consumes untrusted input from the environment it operates in.

  • Experience integrating ML into production, multi-tenant SaaS, or running ML systems in customer-controlled or air-gapped environments.

 

Perks of Horizon3

  • Inclusive Team: We value diversity and promote an inclusive culture where everyone can thrive.

  • Growth Opportunities: Be part of a dynamic and growing team with numerous career development opportunities.

  • Innovative Culture: Work in a collaborative environment that encourages creativity and out-of-the-box thinking.

  • Hybrid & Remote Work: We embrace a mix of remote and hybrid work models depending on role and location, including our Chicago office, where some roles require regular in-office presence.

  • Competitive Compensation: We offer competitive salary, equity and benefits. Our benefits include health, vision & dental insurance for you and your family, a flexible vacation policy, and generous parental leave.

Compensation and Values

At Horizon3, we believe that our people are our greatest asset, and our compensation philosophy reflects this core value. We are committed to fostering an environment where all employees feel valued, respected, and rewarded for their contributions. Our compensation structure is designed to be fair, competitive, and transparent, ensuring that every team member is recognized and compensated equitably across roles, levels, and locations.

In accordance with various State’s transparency regulations, we provide the following salary range information for this position:

  • Base salary range: $313,000 - $369,000 annually. The exact salary will be determined based on the selected candidate’s location, qualifications, experience, and relevant skills.

  • Additional compensation: All full-time roles are eligible for an equity package in the form of stock options.

We are dedicated to fostering a workplace where everyone feels welcome and respected, regardless of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, or any other legally protected status by law.

jobs.description_html:
Get to Know Us

Horizon3 is a fast-growing, remote cybersecurity company dedicated to the mission of enabling organizations to proactively find and fix and verify exploitable attack vectors before criminals exploit them. Our flagship product, the NodeZeroTM platform, delivers production-safe autonomous pentests and other key assessment operations that scale across the largest internal, external, cloud, and hybrid cloud environments. NodeZero has been adopted by organizations of all sizes, from small educational institutions to government agencies and Global 100 enterprises. It is used by ITOps/SecOps teams, consulting pentesters, and MSSPs and MSPs. 

We are a fusion of former U.S. Special Operations cyber operators, startup engineers, and formerly frustrated cybersecurity practitioners. We're committed to helping solve our common security problems: ineffective security tools, false positives resulting in alert fatigue, blind spots, "checkbox” security culture, cybersecurity skills shortage, and the long lead time and expense of hiring outside consultants. Collectively, we are a team of learn it alls, committed to a culture of respect, collaboration, ownership, and results.

 

What You’ll Do

We are looking for an Engineering Manager to build and lead Horizon3’s Developer Experience (DevEx) team. DevEx makes it fast, safe, and easy for engineers to get a change from local development through build, test, and release. The team owns the shared developer workflows and delivery foundations that product teams consume—not the product code or service outcomes those workflows support.

You will:

  • Build, coach, and grow a high-performing Developer Experience team. Set clear expectations, provide regular feedback, support career development, manage performance, and create an inclusive, psychologically safe environment where the team can do its best work.

  • Own the team’s strategy, quarterly roadmap, and delivery commitments. Balance developer-facing improvements with operational health, security, support, migrations, and technical debt; make capacity and trade-offs visible.

  • Treat developer workflows as a product: learn where engineers encounter friction, prioritize the highest-value shared problems, establish clear platform contracts, and drive adoption through usable defaults, documentation, migration support, and feedback.

  • Lead the evolution of the path from repository checkout to production release, including local development, onboarding, repository templates, CI/CD infrastructure, build and test systems, runner configuration, artifact promotion, release manifests, deployment mechanics, gates, and rollback paths.

  • Improve build and pipeline speed, reliability, and feedback quality. Establish useful measures for pipeline health, queue and cycle time, release performance, adoption, and developer experience.

  • Establish sustainable practices for shared container base images, dependency hygiene, reproducible builds, scanning, signing, provenance, and software supply-chain security in partnership with Security and service teams.

  • Promote responsible use of approved AI-assisted development workflows. Ensure generated code receives human review and the same testing, quality, and security checks as other code; protect credentials, secrets, and customer security data.

  • Partner closely with the Cloud Infrastructure manager: DevEx owns developer-facing workflows and configuration of the shared delivery experience; Infrastructure owns the underlying cloud, network, identity, runtime, and delivery-system compute primitives.

  • Work with senior and staff engineers on technical direction, design quality, and cross-team execution without becoming an implementation bottleneck. Align with application, platform, Data Engineering, Security, Product, and Program Management partners.

  • Hire and onboard engineers, contribute to interview calibration, and develop technical owners so shared workflows have durable ownership and coverage.

What You’ll Bring

  • 2+ years experience leading an engineering team and 9+ years as an individual contributor

  • Proven experience in coaching, performance, hiring, and the team’s delivery and health.

  • A strong background in Developer Experience, Developer Productivity, Build/Release Engineering, Platform Engineering, DevOps, or software engineering with substantial developer-tooling or delivery-system ownership.

  • Experience setting a team roadmap, making prioritization and capacity trade-offs, and delivering shared capabilities across teams with different needs.

  • Technical judgment across CI/CD, build systems, developer workflows, container images, artifact handling, release safety, and software supply-chain security.

  • A track record of improving the usability, reliability, security, and adoption of internal platforms or engineering workflows.

  • Experience operating shared systems through failure, using evidence to diagnose issues, choosing safe mitigations, communicating clearly, and driving durable follow-up.

  • Ability to distinguish reusable platform responsibilities from application-team ownership, and to resolve dependencies with infrastructure, Security, and SRE partners.

  • Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to explain trade-offs and outcomes to engineers and non-technical partners.

Required Tech Stack Experience

  • GitLab CI/CD or comparable pipeline systems, including shared components and runner fleets.

  • Docker or OCI images, container build systems, artifact repositories, and reproducible build practices.

  • Kubernetes or comparable cloud-native development and delivery workflows.

  • Automated tests, quality and security gates, artifact promotion, progressive delivery, and rollback.

  • Software supply-chain practices, including dependency and image scanning, signing or provenance, and least-privilege access.

  • Go or Python for automation and developer tooling.

  • Observability for pipelines, builds, releases, and shared developer-platform components.

Exact tool matches are less important than strong software-engineering fundamentals, empathy for developers, sound delivery judgment, and a track record of building systems that teams trust and adopt.

What You'll Do:

Horizon3 is investing in a company-wide data strategy to make our data trusted, governed, and built to power revenue growth. The Federal Senior Product Analytics Engineer sits at the center of that effort: you're the bridge between how product data is modeled and built and how it's trusted and used across the company with a specific focus on our growing Federal business and platforms.

You'll work hand-in-hand with Data Engineering to help shape the canonical product data layer at the source, with the emerging Data Governance function to get metrics certified and documented, and with the Product analysts and PMs to turn that foundation into self-service, decision-ready data products. You're equally comfortable writing a dbt model, troubleshooting a pipeline, and helping a non-technical stakeholder define a company wide KPI.

  • Design, build, and maintain scalable ELT pipelines and data models that translate raw product usage and event telemetry into trusted, well-documented analytics assets.

  • Partner with Product Engineering on the canonical product data layer — ensuring product usage cohorts and behavioral signal definitions are built on accurate, governed source data, not just what's convenient downstream.

  • Build and own the semantic layer and self-service data models for Product Analytics, so internal stakeholders can query with confidence without needing a SQL expert in the room every time.

  • Own data quality monitoring and anomaly detection for product usage data specifically, partnering with Data Engineering when issues trace back to pipeline or platform-level causes.

  • Contribute analytics engineering support to the expansion/upsell cohort work, building the pipelines and models that turn usage thresholds, feature adoption, and seat utilization into certified, production-grade metrics.

  • Present technical data concepts and their business implications clearly to both engineering and non-technical stakeholders, including leadership.

jobs.description_html:
Get to Know Us

Horizon3.ai is a fast-growing, remote cybersecurity company dedicated to the mission of enabling organizations to proactively find, fix and verify exploitable attack vectors before criminals exploit them. Our flagship product, the NodeZero™ platform, delivers production-safe autonomous pentests and other key assessment operations that scale across the largest internal, external, cloud, and hybrid cloud environments. NodeZero has been adopted by organizations of all sizes, from small educational institutions to government agencies and Global 100 enterprises. It is used by IT Ops/SecOps teams, consulting pentesters, and MSSPs and MSPs.

We are a fusion of former U.S. Special Operations cyber operators, startup engineers & operators, and formerly frustrated cybersecurity practitioners. We're committed to helping solve our common security problems: ineffective security tools and false positives, resulting in alert fatigue, blind spots, "checkbox" security culture, cybersecurity skills shortage, and the long lead time and expense of hiring outside consultants. Collectively, we are a team of learn-it-alls, committed to a culture of respect, collaboration, ownership, and results.

As a remote first company, we require minimum 25Mbps consumer grade broadband connection.

 

What You'll Do

The Principal Engineer for Database Platform is the technical anchor of NodeZero's data infrastructure. This is an individual contributor role with no direct reports — your influence is through technical leadership, architecture ownership, and raising the engineering bar across the team. You own the most consequential database architecture decisions, define the standards that govern how NodeZero stores, queries, and migrates data at scale, and ensure the data layer can support NodeZero's growth — more customers, larger environments, more pentest data — without requiring proportional operational effort. This is a deeply hands-on role: you will write code, author design documents, and set the technical direction that every engineer on the Database Platform team builds toward.

NodeZero's data layer is not simple. We store millions of discovered assets, graph-structured attack paths, time-series vulnerability data, and audit-critical pentest results — across a multi-tenant architecture where correctness and data isolation are non-negotiable. You will be the person who makes the hardest data architecture calls and ensures the team has the technical foundations to build reliably on.

  • Technical Strategy: Define and drive the technical roadmap for the Database Platform in partnership with the Senior Engineering Manager and the broader Pentest Platform organization.

  • Architecture Leadership: Own the most complex database architecture decisions — schema design, partitioning strategies, migration patterns, and scalability approaches. Produce design documents that become the shared technical model for the team.

  • PostgreSQL Excellence: Be NodeZero's definitive expert on PostgreSQL at scale — query optimization, indexing, partitioning, replication, and connection pooling. Set the standards the team follows and catch the problems others miss.

  • Graph & Multi-model Data: Architect and guide the evolution of NodeZero's graph-based asset model — the data structure that represents how discovered hosts, services, credentials, and vulnerabilities relate to each other across pentests.

  • Schema Governance: Own schema design review processes. Ensure every migration is safe, reversible, and zero-downtime. Build the tooling and culture that treats schema changes with the same rigor as production code changes.

  • Mentorship & Bar Raising: Mentor P5 and P4 engineers through code review, design review, and pairing. Be the person on the team that raises everyone else's ceiling.

  • Cross-functional Influence: Partner with Data Ingestion, Asset Inventory, API Platform, and Security Research to define data contracts, query performance standards, and architectural guardrails that span the full data pipeline.

 

What You'll Bring

Technical Depth

  • Deep, production-proven PostgreSQL expertise: query planner internals, advanced indexing (partial, expression, GiST/GIN), partitioning strategies, logical replication, vacuuming at scale, and connection pool tuning.

  • Experience architecting multi-tenant databases at scale: row-level security, tenant isolation, schema-per-tenant vs. shared-schema tradeoffs.

  • Experience with schema migration at scale in production systems: zero-downtime migrations, backwards-compatible schema evolution, and migration tooling (Flyway, golang-migrate, or equivalent).

  • Familiarity with graph data models and graph databases (Neo4j, AWS Neptune) or graph-like query patterns in relational systems (recursive CTEs, ltree, adjacency list).

  • Proficient in Go or Python — able to write production application code, not just SQL.

Architecture & Design

  • Demonstrated track record of defining database architecture at scale — from design doc to production — across multiple companies or teams.

  • Strong opinions on data architecture tradeoffs: normalization vs. denormalization, consistency vs. availability, OLTP vs. OLAP workload separation, and schema-first vs. schema-last design.

  • Able to reason about long-horizon schema design: what does this schema look like in two years, at 10× the current data volume, with three new feature teams writing to it?

  • Able to communicate complex database decisions clearly in writing — for design docs, ADRs, and cross-team reviews — so engineers without deep DB expertise can understand and apply the reasoning.

Leadership Without Authority

  • Proven ability to drive database standards across multiple teams without direct reporting authority — including teams that are not the Database Platform team.

  • Experience establishing database engineering culture: schema review norms, migration safety standards, and query performance review processes.

  • Track record of growing engineers through code review, pair programming, and architectural mentorship — especially engineers who are strong in application code but earlier in their database expertise.

 

Nice to Haves

  • Background in cybersecurity data: vulnerability databases, network scan schemas, or attack surface management data models.

  • Experience with time-series databases (TimescaleDB, InfluxDB) in addition to relational.

  • Familiarity with data platform compliance requirements: SOC 2 Type II, FedRAMP data handling, or GDPR/CCPA.

  • Experience with analytical query patterns or BI/reporting workloads on operational data.

  • Contributions to open-source database tooling or PostgreSQL ecosystem projects.

 

Travel Required

We are a fully remote company, and this job may require up to 5% of travel to be successful.

 

Compensation and Values

We are committed to fostering an environment where all employees feel valued, respected, and rewarded for their contributions. Our compensation structure is designed to be fair, competitive, and transparent, ensuring that every team member is recognized and compensated equitably across roles, levels, and locations.

In accordance with various State's transparency regulations, we provide the following salary range information for this position:

The ideal candidate has carried and exceeded a multi-million dollar civilian quota, knows the difference between an enthusiastic program office and a funded program of record, and can navigate the authorization, procurement, and partner layers that determine whether a federal deal actually closes. You will own your agency portfolio as a business: named account plans, sponsor and champion maps, a partner strategy, and a forecast you can defend line by line.

This role will be responsible for:

  • Own a named portfolio of cabinet-level civilian agencies and their component bureaus, carrying an annual net-new ARR quota with defined expansion and renewal-protection targets.

  • Develop mission-aligned account plans for each agency in the portfolio that connect NodeZero outcomes to specific mission systems, funded programs, named sponsors, and a viable path to production.

  • Prospect and generate self-sourced pipeline into agency CISO, ISSO, SOC, vulnerability management, RMF/ATO, and program-office stakeholders, rather than relying on inbound or marketing-sourced demand.

  • Qualify against federal buying reality — active mission need, named sponsor, identified funding, and a clear authorization and contract path — and disqualify early when those conditions are absent.

  • Run proof of value engagements in partnership with Federal Sales Engineering, converting technical validation into a documented business case, procurement action, and executive-level readout.

  • Position NodeZero Federal against the mandates your buyers already live under, including CISA BOD 26-04, OMB M-22-09 and the Federal Zero Trust Strategy, FISMA, NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, NIST SP 800-207, and CDM — translating audit and POA&M burden into validated, evidence-based risk reduction.

  • Navigate federal procurement end to end, selecting and executing through the appropriate vehicle (GSA schedules, GWACs/IDIQs, SEWP, P1 Marketplace, BPAs, agency-specific contracts) and managing quoting, sole-source justification, and small-business set-aside considerations with RevOps, Legal, and Finance.

  • Build and monetize channel and integrator relationships across distributors, FedRAMP-aware resellers, and systems integrators — treating partners as accelerators who bring contract access, agency relationships, and capture support, not as a passive fulfillment layer.

  • Maintain accurate, current, and defensible pipeline hygiene in Salesforce: realistic close dates, documented next steps, stage discipline, and forecast commitments that hold up under weekly and quarterly inspection.

  • Deliver a weekly forecast and quarterly business review covering pipeline generation by source, stage conversion, slipped deals, closed-lost reasons, and net-new versus renewal ARR.

  • Represent Horizon3 credibly in front of agency leadership, at federal industry events, and in partner-led forums, and feed field intelligence on requirements, competitors, and authorization gaps back to Product, Marketing, and Federal Engineering.

  • Protect and expand existing civilian customer relationships in coordination with Customer Success and Renewals, driving usage, referenceability, and multi-year commitments.

What You'll Bring

  • Must have a demonstrated track record of selling enterprise cybersecurity or SaaS solutions directly to U.S. federal civilian agencies, with consistent quota overachievement against a multi-million dollar number.

  • 8+ years of quota-carrying enterprise technology sales experience, with 5+ years selling into U.S. federal civilian agencies.

  • 3+ years of experience selling cybersecurity, INFOSEC, or security SaaS solutions.

  • Must have existing, verifiable relationships across multiple cabinet-level civilian agencies and their component bureaus, and the ability to describe those agencies' mission priorities, buying cycles, and organizational structures in specifics rather than generalities.

  • Deep understanding of federal procurement mechanics, including contract vehicles (GSA, GWACs/IDIQs, SEWP, BPAs), fiscal-year and end-of-year budget dynamics, appropriations timing, and the role of distributors, resellers, and systems integrators in a federal transaction.

  • Knowledgeable in the federal compliance and authorization landscape that shapes civilian security spend — FedRAMP, FISMA, RMF and the ATO process, NIST SP 800-53, Zero Trust and OMB M-22-09, CDM, POA&M workflows, and CISA binding operational directives.

  • Working understanding of offensive security and vulnerability management concepts — penetration testing, attack paths, lateral movement, privilege escalation, Active Directory weaknesses, and the practical limits of scanner-based vulnerability programs — sufficient to lead a credible technical conversation without an SE in the room.

  • Proficient in managing the full sales cycle end to end: prospecting, qualification, proof of value, business case development, negotiation, procurement execution, and close.

  • Proficient in Salesforce for pipeline, forecast, and activity management, and comfortable with a sales stack that includes tools such as Outreach.io, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, ZoomInfo, Gong, and Slack.

  • Able to operate with a high degree of autonomy in an early-stage federal business — building process where none exists, working across a distributed and cross-functional team, and moving with urgency and ownership.

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to brief agency executives and authorizing officials on risk and mission impact rather than features.

Minimum education and experience requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Information Technology, Cybersecurity, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

  • Must reside in or relocate to the DC Metro area.

Work Authorization & Security Clearance Requirements

Only US persons can interview for this role due to security clearance requirements by our customer(s) and/or vendor(s). While a clearance is not required to perform the core responsibilities of this role, the employee must be eligible for and able to successfully secure a US Federal Security Clearance if required by a specific customer program or engagement.

What Sets You Apart?

  • Experience selling offensive security, penetration testing, breach and attack simulation, continuous threat exposure management (CTEM), or security validation solutions into federal customers.

  • Experience being the first or one of the first sellers into a civilian agency — opening a stale or greenfield account and building it into a program-level relationship.

  • Experience selling a FedRAMP-authorized SaaS platform, including guiding an agency through package review, agency ATO, and production deployment.

  • Knowledge of the civilian systems integrator and prime ecosystem, and a track record of using those relationships to reach mission owners and accelerate contract access.

  • Prior experience as a government civilian, military member, or federal contractor, particularly in a cybersecurity, IT operations, or program management capacity.

  • Familiarity with Challenger or question-based selling methodologies and a disciplined approach to MEDDPICC-style qualification.

  • Experience selling into public-facing citizen services and mission application environments where appsec and testing budgets already exist.

Travel Required

Collectively, we are a team of learn it alls, committed to a culture of respect, collaboration, ownership, and results.

What You'll Do

As a Senior Full-Stack Engineer on the Autonomous Defensive team, you'll build the platform that NodeZero's defensive agents run on. Our AI researchers define what these agents should reason about, you build the systems that make that work in production, across thousands of customer tenants, without breaking anything.

That means real distributed systems problems, not glue code. They execute inside customer environments under tight isolation, credential, and egress constraints. And when an agent proposes a change in production, the platform has to be able to simulate it, stage it, gate it on approval, roll it back, and prove after the fact exactly what happened and on whose authority.

It also means the interfaces that sit on top of all of that. Autonomous systems are only trusted to the extent that people can see what they did and intervene before they do it, and that burden lands on the front end. These surfaces are part of the product, not a thin layer over the API, and you'll own them end to end alongside the backend they talk to.

This is a platform role. You'll own the runtime, the tool layer, the orchestration, the connector framework, and the observability and UI that make agent behavior debuggable. We're looking for engineers with strong backend depth who are comfortable building the front end when the workflow demands it — not because it's beneath them, but because they understand the value of end-to-end delivery. You'll work closely with our AI researchers, but you are not being hired to tune prompts — you are being hired to build the substrate that makes their work shippable and safe.

Responsibilities

  • Build and own the agent execution runtime: durable, resumable, long-running workflows with checkpointing, idempotent steps, cancellation, and timeouts at both the step and run level.

  • Design and implement the tool layer that agents act through — a registry with versioning, schema validation, per-tenant enablement, and authorization enforced server-side rather than by the model.

  • Build the connector framework for third-party security control planes (EDR, firewall, identity, SIEM, cloud IAM).

  • Implement the safe-change pipeline: dry-run and simulation, blast-radius classification, approval gates for high-impact actions, staged rollout, rollback, and an immutable per-tenant audit trail.

  • Build the operator-facing front end in React and TypeScript, turning dense system state into interfaces a user can reason about and act on with confidence.

  • Build the client-side data and streaming layer that keeps those interfaces accurate against long-running, incrementally updating state, over WebSockets rather than polling.

  • Extend NodeZero's tenant isolation model to agents that take write actions, covering execution boundaries, egress control, quotas, and cross-tenant leakage in caches, indexes, and logs.

  • Develop core product features in ETL and GraphQL to support data processing and retrieval for agent context, run history, and remediation state.

  • Build the ETL pipelines that turn pentest and remediation outcomes into the datasets our researchers train and evaluate against.

  • Instrument everything. Distributed tracing across an agent run, cost and token accounting per tenant, and the tooling to answer "why did the agent do that" without guessing.

  • Partner with AI researchers, attack engineers, and product to take capabilities from prototype to production, and feed platform constraints back into research direction early rather than late.

Required Education / Experience

  • Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering or related field.

  • 7+ yrs professional software engineering experience using modern object-oriented or functional languages (Python, Go, Scala, C++, TypeScript, etc).

  • Proven experience delivering backend APIs, especially GraphQL, and consuming them from a modern web stack.

  • Production experience with React, TypeScript, and modern CSS layout, with the judgment to build a usable interface for a complex workflow without a designer holding your hand.

  • Experience building applications on cloud computing platforms such as AWS, Azure, GCP, using container technologies such as Docker and Kubernetes.

  • Expert proficiency in SQL.

  • Demonstrated experience designing and operating distributed systems in production: asynchronous workflows, queues, retries, idempotency, and partial failure.

  • A track record of shipping and operating production services, including on-call ownership.

What Sets You Apart

  • Experience building agentic or LLM-backed systems in production

  • Experience with a durable execution (such as Temporal) or workflow engine or having built equivalent checkpointing yourself.

  • Experience building multi-tenant platforms with hard isolation requirements, workload identity, and short-lived credential brokering.

  • Experience integrating a long tail of third-party APIs behind a normalized abstraction.

  • Familiarity with security control planes and their APIs — EDR (CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Microsoft Defender), firewalls, SIEM, cloud IAM.

  • Experience with database architectures including relational (PostgreSQL) and graph (Neo4j), and experience building GraphQL backends.

  • Experience with client-side data and streaming patterns — React Query or Apollo, GraphQL subscriptions, WebSockets — against long-running, incrementally updating state.

  • Experience building operator-facing or admin interfaces where density, auditability, and getting the destructive action right matter more than visual polish.

  • Experience with observability tooling (Datadog, Prometheus, Grafana) and distributed tracing.

  • Awareness of prompt injection and untrusted-input handling in systems where an agent consumes data from the environment it operates in.

Travel Required

We are a fully remote company, and this job may require up to 5% of travel to be successful.

Compensation and Values

jobs.description_html:

NodeZero has been adopted by organizations of all sizes, from small educational institutions to government agencies and Global 100 enterprises. It is used by ITOps/SecOps teams, consulting pentesters, and MSSPs and MSPs. 

We are a fusion of former U.S. Special Operations cyber operators, startup engineers, and formerly frustrated cybersecurity practitioners. We're committed to helping solve our common security problems: ineffective security tools, false positives resulting in alert fatigue, blind spots, "checkbox” security culture, cybersecurity skills shortage, and the long lead time and expense of hiring outside consultants. Collectively, we are a team of learn it alls, committed to a culture of respect, collaboration, ownership, and results.

About the Role

Horizon3.ai is building a Strategy & Programs function within Revenue Operations to help the organization successfully execute its highest-priority cross-functional initiatives as we continue to scale.

We are looking for a RevOps Program Manager to lead complex initiatives that span Revenue Operations and the broader business. This role will partner closely with teams including Sales Operations, Systems Operations, Deal Desk, Customer Operations, Partner Operations, Finance, Product, Engineering, Marketing, and other cross-functional stakeholders.

This is not a traditional IT Project Manager role, nor is it a project coordinator position. The ideal candidate combines strong program management discipline with business acumen, sound judgment, and the ability to create structure in ambiguous environments.

You will be responsible for turning strategic priorities into executable plans, aligning stakeholders around decisions and outcomes, identifying and managing risks and dependencies, and driving initiatives from definition through implementation.

As an early member of the Strategy & Programs team, you will also have the opportunity to help establish how project management operates within Revenue Operations as the function grows.

What You'll Do

Lead Strategic Initiatives

  • Lead moderately complex, cross-functional initiatives from initial scoping through implementation and closeout with little to no day-to-day direction.

  • Translate strategic priorities and business objectives into clear project plans, milestones, workstreams, dependencies, and success measures.

  • Establish appropriate project governance, operating cadences, decision-making structures, and stakeholder engagement models.

  • Manage multiple concurrent initiatives across different areas of the Revenue Operations organization.

  • Maintain accountability across project teams while recognizing that functional leaders and subject-matter experts retain ownership of functional decisions and outcomes.

Drive Cross-Functional Execution

  • Coordinate work across Revenue Operations functions including Sales Operations, Systems Operations, Deal Desk, Customer Operations, and Partner Operations, as well as teams across the broader organization.

  • Facilitate effective working sessions, project meetings, leadership reviews, and decision-making forums.

  • Proactively identify dependencies, risks, blockers, and competing priorities and drive them toward resolution.

  • Establish clear owners, decisions, and next steps across project workstreams.

  • Escalate issues appropriately when additional leadership direction or decision-making is required.

  • Build alignment across teams with different priorities, perspectives, and areas of expertise.

Provide Project Governance & Visibility

  • Maintain project plans, milestones, risks, dependencies, decisions, and action items.

  • Develop concise, executive-ready project updates that communicate progress, risks, decisions required, and overall project health.

  • Ensure leadership has appropriate visibility into strategic initiatives without creating unnecessary administrative overhead.

  • Support portfolio-level visibility across active Strategy & Programs initiatives.

  • Help establish repeatable project management standards, templates, and governance practices for the organization.

Support Business & Operational Transformation

Projects may include initiatives such as:

  • Sales process and operating model changes

  • Territory, segmentation, and coverage initiatives

  • Pricing and packaging rollouts

  • Partner and channel program launches

  • Customer lifecycle improvements

  • Quote-to-Cash transformation

  • Revenue technology implementations

  • CRM and GTM systems initiatives

  • Systems integrations and automation

  • New GTM motions and commercialization programs

  • Data and reporting initiatives

  • Process redesign and operational scalability initiatives

The specific portfolio will evolve based on business priorities. Program Managers are expected to operate across both business-oriented and technology-enabled initiatives rather than being permanently assigned to a single Revenue Operations function.

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years of project, program, business operations, Revenue Operations, or related experience leading cross-functional initiatives.

  • Demonstrated ability to independently manage moderately complex projects from scoping through implementation.

  • Experience working in a high-growth SaaS, technology, or similarly fast-paced environment.

  • Strong project planning, organization, prioritization, and risk-management skills.

  • Strong business acumen and the ability to quickly understand unfamiliar business processes and operating models.

  • Demonstrated ability to lead through influence rather than formal authority.

  • Experience coordinating stakeholders across multiple functions and levels of an organization.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience communicating project status, risks, and recommendations to senior leaders.

  • Ability to identify problems, evaluate tradeoffs, exercise sound judgment, and drive teams toward practical solutions.

  • Comfortable operating in ambiguity and creating structure where processes or requirements may not yet be fully defined.

  • Ability to balance project management rigor with the speed and pragmatism required in a high-growth environment.

Experience That Could Make You Successful

We expect successful candidates to come from a variety of backgrounds. Experience in one or more of the following areas is valuable:

  • Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, Customer Operations, Partner Operations, Deal Desk, or Business Operations

  • Cross-functional GTM initiatives or commercial transformation

  • Business systems or revenue technology implementations

  • CRM, CPQ, CLM, ERP, or other enterprise technology programs

  • Product or Engineering partnership

  • Process improvement and operating model design

  • Change management and organizational transformation

  • Data, analytics, or data governance initiatives

What Success Looks Like

Successful Program Managers within Strategy & Programs:

  • Turn ambiguous business priorities into clear, executable plans.

  • Create accountability without adding unnecessary bureaucracy.

  • Anticipate risks and dependencies rather than simply reporting them after they occur.

  • Drive timely decisions and maintain momentum across cross-functional teams.

  • Build trust with both business and technical stakeholders.

  • Give leaders clear visibility into project health, tradeoffs, and decisions required.

  • Help initiatives achieve their intended business outcomes while ensuring sustainable transition to the appropriate functional owners.

  • Continuously improve how Revenue Operations plans and delivers complex initiatives.

Who You Are

You are highly organized without being overly process-driven. You are comfortable walking into an initiative where not everything has been figured out yet and helping the team establish a path forward.

You ask good questions, learn unfamiliar areas quickly, and understand when to facilitate, when to challenge, and when to escalate. You are equally comfortable working with detailed project teams and communicating with senior leadership.

Most importantly, you view program management as more than maintaining timelines and scheduling meetings. You see the role as helping teams turn complex business decisions into coordinated, measurable execution.

  • Competitive Compensation: We offer competitive salary, equity and benefits. Our benefits include health, vision & dental insurance for you and your family, a flexible vacation policy, and generous parental leave.

Compensation and Values

About the Team

Revenue Strategy & Operations is the team behind how Horizon3's go-to-market organization is planned, run and measured. We own budgeting and headcount planning, quota and compensation, territory planning and management (accounts, opportunities, leads and routing), goals for pipeline and performance, forecasting, performance management, and the operating process the sales organization runs on. Regional partners carry that scope for their sales leaders in AMER, EMEA and APJ. Global Centers of Excellence set the standards they all run on. This role sits on the AMER team, which carries that scope for the Americas sales organization, the largest in the company.

About the Role

We are hiring a Senior Revenue Strategy & Operations Manager, AMER to join our Americas team during a period of fast growth. You will run the operating cadence for your assigned segments, own the analysis behind forecasting and planning, and make sure the territories, data and reporting AMER sales leaders rely on are accurate and trusted.

This is a senior individual contributor role with end-to-end ownership. You will work directly with first-line and second-line sales leaders and their teams, act as the backup for AMER Revenue Strategy & Operations leadership, and help build an operating model that scales with the business. You run on the global standards our Centers of Excellence set for planning, process and compensation, and you have a hand in improving them.

The role takes high agency: think for yourself, dive into ambiguity, and drive work through to done.

What You'll Do

Run the Rhythm of the Business

  • Run the weekly forecast and pipeline review cadence for your segments: the inspection views, call-outs and roll-ups leaders use to call the number.

  • Own pipeline and performance analytics for your segments, including coverage, pipeline creation, conversion, velocity, win rates and rep productivity, and turn the analysis into clear narratives for monthly and quarterly business reviews.

  • Partner day to day with first-line and second-line sales leaders and the overlay leaders in your segments, resolving issues and anticipating what they need next.

  • Deploy the pipeline and performance goals set for your segments, track them by team and rep, and flag early when a team is off pace.

  • Serve as backup to AMER Revenue Strategy & Operations leadership across forecast, review and planning activities.

Execute Planning, Territories and Quotas

  • Provide the capacity, productivity and territory inputs for annual and in-year planning, pressure-test the plan for your segments, and deploy it when it comes back.

  • Run territory and account assignment for your segments: annual carves, mid-year changes, new-hire territories, account moves and routing, through the global change process so Salesforce, routing and reporting match what the field expects.

  • Apply the global rules of engagement day to day: account ownership and crediting questions, exceptions, and the recurring issues that should go to Core Operations as policy candidates.

  • Deploy quotas and issue quota letters, and support crediting validation and dispute research with Sales Compensation and Finance.

  • Keep an auditable record of territory, routing and crediting decisions so changes can be traced and repeated.

Own Data Quality and Reporting

  • Hold the data quality standards for your segments: regular audits, dashboards and follow-through with reps and managers.

  • Manage Salesforce records at scale for your segments: accounts, opportunities, ownership, hierarchies and territories, including controlled bulk updates and merges.

  • Build and maintain the reports and dashboards your leaders use on top of the standard reporting, and route data model, routing and workflow changes to GTM Systems through Core Operations.

  • Monitor lead and deal registration routing exceptions, diagnose root causes across data, process and system logic, and drive permanent fixes.

  • Work across Salesforce, Gong, ZoomInfo and related tools to keep your segments' data accurate and usable.

Solve Problems and Improve How AMER Operates

  • Use a structured approach to operational problems: define the issue, quantify the impact, find the root cause, align the stakeholders, fix it and confirm it worked.

  • Lead projects that improve sales effectiveness, planning accuracy and data quality for your segments.

  • Simplify processes and remove manual hand-offs, one-off workarounds and repeated questions, using automation and approved AI tools where they cut manual work without losing control of the data.

  • Document what you build so improvements outlast the person who built them, and share standards and practices with the EMEA and APJ teams.

What We Look For

  • 5 to 8 years in Sales Operations, Revenue Operations or a closely related analytical role in B2B SaaS.

  • Sales operations expertise: You have run or supported forecasting and pipeline inspection, managed territories and account assignments, and deployed quotas and goals for a sales team.

  • Salesforce and data fluency: Strong Salesforce skills across opportunity management, reporting, territory and ownership data and data governance, including managing records at scale and troubleshooting routing and reporting issues. Experience with Gong, ZoomInfo, Everstage or BI tools is a plus.

  • Analytical rigor: You turn operational data into short, clear insights for leaders, and you notice when a number is off before they do.

  • Partnership: You have worked directly with sales leaders and earned their trust as a credible, responsive partner.

  • High agency: You think for yourself, dive into ambiguity, own work end to end and drive it through to done.

  • Experience with Enterprise, Mid-Market or high-velocity segments, or with partner, channel or MSSP motions, is a plus.

What Success Looks Like

  • Leaders in your segments have a reliable, timely view of forecast, pipeline, territories and performance, and they get it from you before they ask.

  • The forecast roll-up matches what the leaders say on the call, every week.

  • Territory and account changes land right the first time, and the field, Salesforce and reporting agree on who owns what.

  • Every new seller in your segments has a territory, routing and quota in place on their first day.

  • Routing is accurate and measured, and the recurring exceptions you raise turn into fixes or policy.

  • Business review prep is about decisions, not assembling data.

 

Perks of Horizon3

  • Innovative Culture: Work in a collaborative environment that encourages creativity and out-of-the-box thinking.

Compensation and Values

This role requires a strong blend of product leadership, cybersecurity expertise, threat intelligence experience, technical depth, and customer empathy to help organizations quickly understand whether emerging vulnerabilities create real, exploitable risk in their environments.

The Staff Product Manager for Rapid Response will own the product strategy, roadmap, customer experience, and operating model for NodeZero Rapid Response. This leader will partner closely with the Attack Team, Engineering, Data, Design, Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Channel, and Support to define how Horizon3 monitors emerging threats, determines which vulnerabilities matter, maps those threats to customer environments, validates real-world exploitability, and helps customers take action before attackers do.

Responsibilities

Rapid Response Product Strategy & Leadership

  • Own the product vision, strategy, roadmap, and measurable outcomes for NodeZero Rapid Response, helping customers understand and respond to emerging vulnerabilities based on real exploitability and customer-specific risk.

  • Establish the end-to-end operating model for Rapid Response, from initial threat signal through research, prioritization, customer relevance analysis, exploit/test development, notification, remediation, retesting, and verification.

  • Set clear ownership, decision rights, service-level expectations, and operating rhythms across the teams required to deliver Rapid Response at speed.

  • Drive standardization and scalability across Rapid Response research, customer communications, integrations, and operational workflows.

Exploit Intelligence & Coverage Strategy

  • Establish and grow exploit-intelligence relationships with security vendors, researchers, and other relevant intelligence providers to identify emerging Rapid Response opportunities as early as possible.

  • Define the threat intelligence strategy for Rapid Response across vendor advisories, CVEs, CISA KEV, public research, exploit repositories, attacker activity, and other sources of vulnerability and exploit intelligence.

  • Develop a prioritization framework for determining which vulnerabilities warrant immediate Rapid Response coverage based on exploitability, attacker utility, prevalence, customer footprint, potential impact, and evidence of exploitation in the wild.

  • Partner directly with vulnerability researchers and attack engineers to assess exploit prerequisites, affected products and versions, attack techniques, mitigations, and the evidence and production-safety controls needed to validate exploitability in customer environments.

Customer Relevance, Exploitability & Automation

  • Build capabilities that identify which customers, environments, and assets are potentially affected by an emerging threat using asset intelligence, technology fingerprinting, exposure context, historical NodeZero data, and other relevant signals.

  • Drive the product, onboarding, and Customer Success motion required to get 100% of customers to run EAD and keep discovery current so Rapid Response notifications can be relevant and actionable.

  • Drive automation that accelerates exploit and test development, including reusable research and exploit-development workflows, AI-assisted analysis, automated data collection, quality gates, and production-safety checks.

  • Define and monitor operational metrics such as time from disclosure to threat assessment, time to customer relevance determination, time to test availability, alert precision, validation coverage, remediation rates, and retest rates.

Customer Adoption, Growth & Go-to-Market

  • Track Rapid Response test rates by event, customer, segment, and technology to ensure the offering is delivering measurable customer value and to identify adoption gaps that require product or go-to-market action.

  • Own Rapid Response attach-rate analysis and define customer-level triggers for renewals, new ARR, and expansion when an event is relevant to a customer's technology stack, industry, or exposure profile.

  • Partner with Alliances, Channel, and Marketing to turn Rapid Response intelligence and event content into partner plays, enablement, packaging, and campaigns that accelerate attach rates and qualified demand.

  • Define the measurement funnel from threat event to awareness, customer notification, test execution, remediation, pipeline influence, retention, and expansion, and use those insights to improve the product and go-to-market motion.

Cross-Functional Execution, UX & Reporting

  • Own the quality of the Rapid Response user experience and reporting, ensuring customers can quickly understand whether they are affected, see proof, take action, communicate results internally, and confidently demonstrate the value of the product.

  • Define how Rapid Response fits into customer security operations through notifications, APIs, ticketing, SIEM/SOAR, vulnerability management, and other security and IT workflows.

  • Partner with Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Channel, and Support to drive launches, enablement, customer education, adoption, event response, and feedback loops for Rapid Response.

  • Engage directly with CISOs, vulnerability management teams, SOC teams, incident responders, security researchers, prospects, and partners to understand emerging-threat response workflows and unmet needs.

Travel Required

  • Hybrid role is located in San Francisco, New York, or Washington DC. Role may require up to 20% travel to be successful.

Qualifications

  • 7+ years of Product Management experience building deeply technical B2B SaaS products, with significant cybersecurity experience and depth in one or more domains such as vulnerability management, exposure management, offensive security, incident response, SOC operations, attack surface management, endpoint security, or threat detection and response.

  • Threat intelligence experience is required. You have hands-on experience working in or closely with cyber threat intelligence, vulnerability intelligence, threat research, emerging-threat response, or a closely related discipline.

  • Strong technical understanding of the vulnerability and exploitation lifecycle—including CVEs, CISA KEV, vendor advisories, proof-of-concept exploits, exploitation in the wild, affected products and versions, exploit prerequisites, mitigations, and remediation—with enough depth to work directly with vulnerability researchers and attack engineers on safe exploitability validation.

The goal is one plan that top-down and bottom-up both agree with, and one set of numbers leaders trust.

You will work with Finance, Recruiting, Sales leadership and the regional Revenue Strategy & Operations partners. Finance owns the dollars. Recruiting owns the hiring. Sales Compensation owns how quota is constructed. Analytics builds and publishes the reports. The regional partners own the relationship with each sales leader and run the plan in their region. You own the plan, the goals and the model that connect all of it.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role. You build the models, pull the numbers and present them yourself. You need to be as comfortable with the executive team as with a regional sales leader, and able to get people at different levels to commit to the same plan. You will work closely with the Core Operations lead, who owns the standards and processes the organization runs on.

What You'll Do

  • GTM long-range plan: Own the go-to-market side of the long-range plan with Finance: headcount by role and region, hiring timing, ramp, productivity and capacity. Reconcile it to the budget every month so the plan, the roster and the projections tell the same story.

  • Capacity and headcount model: Build and maintain the model that shows how hiring turns into bookings capacity. Keep approved roles and start dates current, and work with Recruiting so the hiring plan and the capacity plan assume the same things.

  • Planning cycle: Run annual and in-year planning end to end: timeline, inputs, decision forums and sign-off. Territories, capacity and quotas are out before the fiscal year starts.

  • Quota allocation: Turn Finance-approved targets into segment, team and role-level quotas based on capacity, territory potential and productivity history. Check that quotas are attainable and fair before they reach the field. Sales Compensation owns how quota is constructed (buffer, proration, ramp, crediting); work with them so allocation and construction run as one method.

  • Goal framework: Set the goals beyond quota that spell out what has to be true globally and in each region: pipeline generation, conversion, SE and top-of-funnel targets agreed with Marketing, Channel and SDR. Keep them consistent so regional goals add up to the global plan.

  • Performance and efficiency metrics: Define the core performance and efficiency metrics, what they mean and how often they are reviewed. Pull and review the numbers, set the reporting calendar and requirements, and sign off that what Analytics publishes measures what the plan set.

  • Planning governance: Own how in-year changes to quota, territory and headcount are requested, approved and recorded, with clear thresholds. Run scenario planning for leadership with the assumptions written down.

  • Global and regional alignment: Be the operating partner to FP&A on heads, capacity and targets, and to the regional partners on their plans. Make sure every region's inputs land in the model, every region gets its plan and quotas back on time, and the global and regional plans tie.

  • 8+ years in GTM planning, sales strategy and operations, revenue operations or sales finance in B2B SaaS, including end-to-end ownership of at least one global annual planning and quota cycle.

Get to Know Us

NodeZero is used by organizations ranging from educational institutions and government agencies to Global 100 enterprises, as well as by ITOps and SecOps teams, consulting pentesters, and MSSPs and MSPs.

We are a team of former U.S. Special Operations cyber operators, startup engineers and operators, and formerly frustrated cybersecurity practitioners.   • Proficiency in troubleshooting challenges using the Linux/Unix command line interface.
  • Possession of recognized Professional Certifications such as RHCE, Linux+, MCSA, AWS Solutions Architect, AWS Developer, Security+, CISSP, and CCNA.
  • Background in DevOps automation practices.

The annual salary range for this role as it is posted is $168,993 - $211,241 regardless of final candidate location within the United States. The final job level and annual salary will be determined based on the education, qualification, knowledge, skills, ability, and experience of the final candidate(s), and calibrated against relevant market data and internal team equity.

We also cover 100% of the premium for employee and dependent Dental and Vision as well as employee premiums for Life and Disability coverage.

In lieu of your $500 annual wellness benefit, you can instead get a $75 monthly credit towards a Life Time membership ($900 annual benefit).
