jobs.title: Sr Growth Manager
jobs.description_html:
Your Dream. Our Team.

About Rise8

Rise8 builds custom, secure software for government organizations, measuring success by impact: lives saved, time returned, and missions advanced. 

We think big, start small, and scale fast with elite teams across product, design, and engineering to drive continuous delivery for critical missions.

We believe customer experience starts with employee experience, so we take care of our employees. Rise8 is where you’ll do the best work of your career—supported by a culture you won’t find anywhere else. We offer competitive pay and benefits, but what sets us apart is our commitment to autonomy, growth, and a culture rooted in kindness, candor, and continuous learning. 

Certified as a Great Place to Work®, with 100% of employees saying they love working here, Rise8 is where bold ideas become real capabilities. Where mission meets meaning. And where fewer bad things happen because of bad software.

Winning the best work is your job. Customer relationships are your specialty.

Software sits between the government and nearly everyone it serves. When it fails, real people pay for it: a service member waiting on a capability they need, a Veteran waiting on care, a family waiting on a tax refund. Each failure also costs something harder to rebuild than software: people’s trust that their government can deliver for them.

Rise8 exists so fewer bad things happen because of bad software.

As a Senior Growth Manager, you are customer facing first. You earn the trust of the government leaders who own a mission, learn how that mission really runs, and find the places where software can change the result. Then you turn those into funded work Rise8 can win and deliver.

You own the distance between a mission problem worth solving and a contract that lets Rise8 solve it. Relationships are your deepest craft. Outcomes are why you’re here.

The job has changed

Most firms in this market grow by account. They pick an agency, watch the forecast, and respond when the solicitation drops. By then, the work that decides the winner is mostly done.

We grow by mission. We start with the mission a government leader is accountable for and the number they report on it. Then we learn everything around it: how the work flows, the systems and programs it depends on, the contracts already in place, and the people who own each piece. Opportunities come out of that understanding, and they come earlier.

AI tools have changed the job too. Market research, contract landscapes, competitive analysis, and first drafts used to take a capture team weeks. One person directing agents can now do them in hours. The tools give you range, but they can’t sit across from a customer, earn trust, or judge which problem is worth pursuing.

That’s where you come in. Less of your week goes to the desk and more goes to the customer. More pipeline isn’t the goal. The right work, won, with outcomes in production, is. We need Growth Managers with the drive to meet new people, the curiosity to understand their world, and the discipline to turn a conversation into outcomes in production.

What Growth Managers do

  • Own the Account Strategy. Set the plan for your agency: which missions to pursue, with what priority, and why. Decide where Rise8 places our bets, and keep the plan current as you learn.
  • Be in front of the customer. This role is customer facing first and foremost. You build and deepen relationships with mission owners, program leaders, end users, and acquisition professionals, in person whenever you can.
  • Understand the mission. Learn how the work flows, where it breaks, which systems and programs it depends on, and who owns each piece. Challenge assumptions, ask probing questions, and help customers rethink how software can improve mission outcomes.
  • Find the gaps worth closing. Turn what you hear into hypotheses. Where could software change how people or systems behave, and move the number the mission owner reports?
  • Generate and qualify opportunities. Build pipeline from relationships, not from a search alert. Qualify hard and early, and walk away from work that doesn’t fit. The goal isn't more deals, it’s more of the right deals.
  • Own your pipeline. Know what's real, what's at risk, and what needs to happen next. Develop, organize, and execute customer call plans. Assess win probability honestly, and keep the CRM current so the forecast reflects reality.
  • Shape the acquisition. Build the relationships and buying intent that turn a good conversation into a real acquisition. Work with customers on how to buy the outcome: the requirement, the contract type, and the path to award. That includes commercial solutions openings, other transactions, and task orders on existing vehicles.
  • Know the landscape. Track budgets, vehicles, recompetes, incumbents, and competitors across your missions. Know who's in the room, what they want, and how Rise8 can win. Find the partners who make a team stronger, and build those relationships before you need them.
  • Lead the pursuit and close. Own the win strategy and bring the right Risers together to make it happen. Work with Solutions, Proposals, Pricing, Contracts, and Delivery to turn customer insight into compelling white papers, demos, proposals, and winning offers. Keep the team moving, clear the obstacles, and get the deal across the finish line.
  • Hand off and keep growing. Work with Customer Success and Delivery so the outcome we sold is the outcome we deliver. Turn what we learn and the trust we earn into follow-on work, deeper relationships, and new opportunities across adjacent missions and organizations.
  • Represent Rise8. Show up where our customers are. Build relationships at industry events, share what we're learning, and help people understand what's possible when software actually works.
  • Put AI to work. Hand research, analysis, and drafting to agents. Review what comes back, catch what’s off, and turn your notes and judgment into reusable context that makes every teammate faster.

How we work when it matters

In government, the stakes are real. These habits come straight from our values, and Growth holds to them the same way our delivery teams do.

Outcomes or bust. A signed contract is a milestone. Prod or it didn’t happen: we count the win when working software reaches users and something measurable changes.

Qualify early and learn fast. We test the riskiest assumptions first. Is there an accountable owner, real budget, and a path to contract? A fast no beats a slow maybe.

Keep it real. We tell customers what we think, including when we aren’t the right fit. We surface bad news on a pursuit early and disagree openly. Then we decide, commit, and move.

Be less certain. We walk in with questions and hypotheses before we walk in with a pitch. The customer knows their mission better than we do, and we act like it.

Lead with context, not control. The best ideas win, not the highest-paid opinion. We give you the context to make great decisions, then trust your judgment to make them.

The Bar

These are the table stakes. We care less about the titles you’ve held and more about what you’ve won, how you shaped it, and what changed for the customer afterward.

  • You’ve won work and can show how. You have a track record of identifying, shaping, and closing federal opportunities. You can walk us through the customer, the problem, the competition, the result, and what a loss taught you.
  • Customers take your call. Your relationships rest on being useful to the people who own the mission, and they last beyond any one contract.
  • You come prepared. You do your homework, know your audience, and sweat the details. You show up to every meeting with a purpose, a plan, and the context to make it count. You communicate early and often, keep people in the loop, and follow through on what you say you'll do. Nothing falls through the cracks.
  • You listen before you pitch. You’re an active listener who asks relevant, probing questions. You leave every meeting knowing more than when you walked in.
  • You know how the government buys. You’ve navigated federal acquisition from budget to award, and you’re comfortable with paths beyond the traditional RFP.
  • You’re credible on software. You don’t need to be an engineer. You understand modern software delivery well enough to spot a real problem, explain why outcomes differ from output, and know when to bring in deeper expertise.
  • You use AI in real work today. You can show how it makes you faster and better prepared, and how you know when to trust the results.
  • You read and write. You read constantly to stay ahead of your customers’ world. You write clearly so teammates and AI agents can understand your thinking and act on it.
  • You own it. You’re self-motivated and entrepreneurial. You act without waiting for perfect instructions, set your own priorities, and follow through on every commitment.
  • You have grit. Federal sales cycles are long, budgets slip, and you will lose some. You learn from it, rethink the approach, and keep going.
  • You find a way. You don't take no for an answer without exploring what's possible. You're creative and resourceful, finding new approaches, opening doors, and keeping momentum when others would wait or walk away. You make things happen instead of waiting for them to happen.
  • You make everyone around you better. You share what you learn, challenge ideas directly, and treat people with kindness and humility.

Your level

Every Growth Manager owns a pipeline and the relationships behind it. What grows with level is the scope you own and how far your influence reaches. Years of experience are a guide, not a gate.

As a Senior Growth Manager, you work autonomously on hard, ambiguous pursuits. Given a customer and a mission, and you figure out where the opportunities are and go win them. Leaders across Rise8 and at partner companies seek out your read on the customer.

Typical experience: Minimum 6 years in federal IT, most of it in business development, capture, or sales.

Pay range: $155,000 to $185,000 Base Salary Plus Annual Incentive Plan

What this role requires

Some missions come with specific requirements from our customers. Here’s what this one needs.

Required

  • Customer: A DoD or VA mission portfolio built around your background. You bring current relationships in at least one service, command, or defense agency, and understand how they buy software.
  • Clearance: Ability to obtain a security clearance for US Government work
  • Citizenship: U.S. citizenship required
  • Location: Remote
  • Travel: Willing to travel up to 25%

Nice to have

  • Experience selling software delivery, digital services, or DevSecOps work to federal customers
  • Wins through commercial solutions openings, other transactions, or SBIR Phase III awards
  • Established relationships with primes and teaming partners in your market
  • Bachelor’s degree in business, marketing, computer science, systems engineering, or a related field

You don’t need to check every box. You need to learn fast, prove your work, and leave things better than you found them. If that sounds like you, come rise with us.

Driven, together, forever, we rise.

Other Benefits 

  • Flexible schedule in a 100% distributed workforce 
  • Premium Insurance: We cover up to 100% of the employee premium and up to 80% of the combined dependent premium on our base health plan, depending on pay band. We also cover 100% of the premium for employee and dependent Dental and Vision as well as employee premiums for Life and Disability coverage.
  • Retirement: 401k match at 10% gross pay.
  • Paid time off (PTO): 4 weeks combined accrued vacation and sick leave, 11 Federal holidays, your birthday, jury duty, and bereavement.
  • Education & Training: Accrued budget of up to $3,500 per year for classes, travel, events, and materials.
  • Home Office and Merch: We offer $750 per year for home office technology and equipment as well as $100 per year for Rise8 merch from our Swag Store.
  • Wellness Budget: To encourage and support a well-rounded healthy lifestyle, we cover 100% reimbursement on a variety of wellness activities and products, up to $500 per calendar year. Or Rise8 is part of the the Life Time Corporate Partner program. In lieu of your $500 annual wellness benefit, you can instead get a $75 monthly credit towards a Life Time membership ($900 annual benefit).
  • Equipment: We offer a MacBook Pro

 

All of Rise8’s work in this area is with Federal Government customers that require our employees involved with their projects be U.S. citizens. As such, this role requires U.S. citizenship. If hired, you would also be required to go through a background investigation.

jobs.title: Agentic AI Engineer
jobs.description_html:
Agentic AI Engineer

AI Engineering | Forward Deployed Engineering

Role Description

Defense Unicorns is seeking an Agentic Engineer to embed with a government team and its technology partners building an emerging AI-powered engineering ecosystem.

This role will focus on designing, integrating, and operationalizing AI agents and agentic workflows within a secure enterprise environment. The engineer will work across large language models, agent frameworks, enterprise data, APIs, developer tooling, and platform services to turn AI capabilities into reliable, mission-relevant workflows.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on engineer who understands both the capabilities and limitations of modern AI systems and can rapidly translate emerging technologies into working solutions. They should be comfortable experimenting with new models and agent frameworks, integrating agents with enterprise systems and tools, evaluating performance and reliability, and working alongside platform engineers and commercial technology partners.

This is not a research-only role. The focus is on moving from AI concepts and prototypes to secure, useful, repeatable agentic capabilities that can operate in production environments.

Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and integrate AI agents and multi-agent workflows using modern LLM and agentic technologies.
  • Develop agent capabilities that interact with enterprise applications, APIs, data sources, developer tools, and mission systems.
  • Integrate models, agents, tools, and enterprise data into secure workflows that can be deployed in controlled and classified environments.
  • Work with LLMs, RAG, embeddings, vector databases, tool/function calling, structured outputs, MCP, and related technologies.
  • Develop mechanisms for agents to securely discover, access, reason over, and act upon approved enterprise data and services.
  • Prototype and rapidly evaluate emerging models, agent frameworks, and AI capabilities to determine where they can create measurable mission or engineering value.
  • Develop evaluation and testing frameworks for agent accuracy, reliability, safety, latency, cost, and task completion.
  • Implement guardrails and policy controls governing agent behavior, tool access, data access, and human approval points.
  • Integrate agentic capabilities with CI/CD and DevSecOps workflows to support repeatable development, testing, deployment, and lifecycle management.
  • Collaborate with platform engineers to operationalize AI workloads within Kubernetes/OpenShift environments.
  • Work with commercial AI and technology partners to integrate their capabilities into the broader engineering ecosystem.
  • Troubleshoot issues across models, agent frameworks, APIs, data sources, networking, identity, and infrastructure.
  • Develop reusable patterns for agent deployment, configuration, observability, evaluation, and lifecycle management.
  • Document architectures, integration patterns, agent specifications, evaluation results, and operational procedures.
  • Identify recurring AI engineering challenges that can be standardized, automated, or productized into reusable capabilities.
  • Stay current with rapidly evolving agentic AI technologies and assess their applicability to secure government environments.

Minimum Experience and Qualifications

  • Active Top Secret clearance.
  • 2-5 years of Hands-on experience building applications or systems using large language models and generative AI.
  • Experience designing and implementing AI agents or agentic workflows.
  • Strong programming experience in Python and/or another modern programming language.
  • Experience integrating AI systems with APIs, enterprise applications, databases, and external tools.
  • Experience with one or more agent frameworks or orchestration approaches.
  • Working knowledge of RAG, embeddings, vector databases, tool/function calling, structured outputs, and prompt engineering.
  • Experience developing software in a Git-based, automated CI/CD environment.
  • Ability to rapidly prototype, test, troubleshoot, and iterate in ambiguous environments.
  • Strong understanding of software engineering fundamentals, including testing, version control, APIs, debugging, and system design.
  • Ability to work effectively alongside platform engineers, government personnel, and multiple technology vendors.

Preferred Experience and Qualifications

  • Experience with MCP (Model Context Protocol) and tool-based agent architectures.
  • Experience with multi-agent systems and agent orchestration.
  • Experience with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, NVIDIA, or comparable foundation model ecosystems.
  • Experience with NVIDIA NIM, NeMo, or similar AI inference/model-serving technologies.
  • Experience with Red Hat OpenShift AI or Kubernetes-based AI platforms.
  • Experience with agent evaluation and observability frameworks.
  • Experience implementing AI guardrails, policy enforcement, human-in-the-loop workflows, or AI safety controls.
  • Experience with LangGraph, LangChain, LlamaIndex, Semantic Kernel, or comparable frameworks.
  • Experience with RAG pipelines, vector databases, knowledge graphs, and enterprise search.
  • Experience deploying AI systems in Secret or TS/SCI environments.
  • Experience with disconnected or air-gapped AI environments.
  • Experience integrating AI into developer/DevSecOps workflows.
  • Familiarity with GitLab, Jira, Confluence, Xacta, or similar enterprise engineering and compliance tools.
  • Experience working with GPUs, model serving, inference optimization, or AI infrastructure.
  • Familiarity with UDS, Zarf, Pepr, Iron Bank, or similar secure software delivery technologies.
  • Experience taking AI prototypes into repeatable, production-ready capabilities.
  • Ability to evaluate new AI technologies quickly and make pragmatic build/buy/integrate decisions.

What Success Looks Like

  • Agentic capabilities move from prototype to mission use quickly, with working agents integrated into real government workflows rather than remaining isolated demos.
  • Agents reliably connect to approved enterprise data, tools, and services, with appropriate identity, permissions, guardrails, and human-in-the-loop controls.
  • AI capabilities are measurable and trustworthy, with repeatable evaluation methods for accuracy, reliability, task completion, security, and operational performance.
  • Reusable agent patterns emerge, reducing the engineering required to build and deploy the next agent or AI-enabled workflow.
  • AI integrates cleanly with the broader platform architecture, working effectively across the data, DevSecOps, Kubernetes/OpenShift, model, and application layers rather than creating another technology silo.
  • The engineer becomes a trusted AI technical advisor to the Mission Hero, proactively identifying where agentic technology can create mission value—and equally important, where AI is not the right solution.

Full compensation packages are based on candidate experience. Compensation ranges are established using national benchmarking data and apply across all geographic locations within the United States.

Defense Unicorns delivers mission value by streamlining software delivery so our customers can focus on the most important challenges. Our commitment to this vision, and to our mission-driven customers, means a commitment to speed, user experience and optionality, without compromising security. jobs.title: Data & AI Engineer (Agentic Systems)
jobs.description_html:
Role Description

Defense Unicorns is seeking an Applied AI Engineer to embed with a government team and its technology partners building an emerging AI-powered engineering ecosystem.

This role will focus on designing, building, and integrating agentic AI capabilities that allow AI models to interact with tools, access enterprise data, execute multi-step workflows, and support mission applications. The engineer will work across LLM integration, agent orchestration, APIs, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and the interfaces between AI applications and existing software platforms.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on software engineer with demonstrated experience building agentic AI applications. They should be comfortable entering an evolving architecture, learning unfamiliar systems quickly, working directly with commercial technology partners, and solving difficult problems involving integration, reliability, performance, and security.

This is not a traditional AI research or model development role. The focus is on building reliable, repeatable agentic capabilities that move beyond experimentation into working software in secure and classified environments.

Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and maintain agentic AI applications that integrate LLMs, tools, APIs, and enterprise data to support mission workflows.
  • Develop AI agents capable of executing multi-step tasks, interacting with external services, and coordinating actions across existing systems.
  • Implement agent orchestration, tool calling, workflow state management, error handling, and appropriate human oversight.
  • Build and integrate RAG pipelines, semantic search, embeddings, and vector-based retrieval to provide relevant context for AI applications.
  • Develop backend services and APIs using Python and modern software engineering practices.
  • Integrate agentic AI capabilities into existing applications, software delivery workflows, and enterprise platforms.
  • Establish testing, evaluation, monitoring, and reliability practices for AI agents and LLM-powered applications.
  • Collaborate with data engineers to ensure agents can access reliable, relevant, and appropriately governed enterprise data.
  • Work with platform engineers to deploy and operate AI applications within Kubernetes/OpenShift environments and integrate them into CI/CD workflows.
  • Troubleshoot end-to-end issues involving agent behavior, tool execution, APIs, data access, application services, and infrastructure.
  • Work directly with government engineers and commercial technology partners to resolve integration challenges and remove blockers to mission delivery.
  • Develop documentation, reusable components, and operational standards that make successful AI implementation patterns repeatable.
  • Operate effectively in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment where technologies, security requirements, and mission priorities continue to evolve.

Local to the National Capital Region and able to support onsite work at a government facility in Springfield, VA as mission needs increase.

Clearance & Travel

  • Active Top Secret clearance with SCI eligibility required
  • Ability to support approximately 2–3 days per week onsite in Springfield, VA, with additional onsite presence as mission needs increase.

Minimum Experience and Qualifications

  • Approximately 3–5 years of software engineering experience, or equivalent demonstrated technical capability.
  • Hands-on experience building agentic AI applications, including AI agents, LLM tool calling, multi-step workflows, or agent orchestration.
  • Strong proficiency with Python and backend software development.
  • Experience integrating LLMs into applications using APIs, SDKs, or comparable technologies.
  • Experience building and integrating REST APIs and connecting applications with external services or data sources.
  • Understanding of agent workflows, tool execution, state management, and error handling.
  • Experience with Git, testing, debugging, and modern software development practices.
  • Experience working in cloud-native or containerized environments and collaborating with platform engineering teams.
  • Ability to troubleshoot application and integration issues across APIs, data services, infrastructure, and AI components.
  • Ability to work independently, rapidly learn new technologies, and translate ambiguous mission needs into working software.
  • GEOINT experience is preferred, not required.

Relevant agentic AI experience may be demonstrated through professional work, internships, research, open-source contributions, or independent projects.

Preferred Experience and Qualifications

  • Experience with agentic AI frameworks such as LangGraph, LangChain, CrewAI, AutoGen, or comparable technologies.
  • Experience developing multi-agent systems, autonomous workflows, or AI-enabled software development tools.
  • Experience with Model Context Protocol (MCP), function calling, or other tool integration patterns.
  • Experience with RAG, embeddings, vector databases, semantic search, or knowledge graphs.

Mission Focus

Make trusted data available where AI needs it, while establishing the repeatable, secure data patterns required to move from experimentation to operational capability.

jobs.title: Senior AI Engineer
jobs.description_html:
Senior Platform Engineer

AI Engineering | Forward Deployed Engineering

Role Description

Defense Unicorns is seeking a senior AI Agentic Engineer to embed with a government team and its technology partners building an emerging AI-powered engineering ecosystem.

This role will focus on designing, integrating, and operationalizing AI agents and agentic workflows within a secure enterprise environment. The engineer will work across large language models, agent frameworks, enterprise data, APIs, developer tooling, and platform services to turn AI capabilities into reliable, mission-relevant workflows.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on engineer who understands both the capabilities and limitations of modern AI systems and can rapidly translate emerging technologies into working solutions. They should be comfortable experimenting with new models and agent frameworks, integrating agents with enterprise systems and tools, evaluating performance and reliability, and working alongside platform engineers and commercial technology partners.

This is not a research-only role. The focus is on moving from AI concepts and prototypes to secure, useful, repeatable agentic capabilities that can operate in production environments.

Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and integrate AI agents and multi-agent workflows using modern LLM and agentic technologies.
  • Develop agent capabilities that interact with enterprise applications, APIs, data sources, developer tools, and mission systems.
  • Integrate models, agents, tools, and enterprise data into secure workflows that can be deployed in controlled and classified environments.
  • Work with LLMs, RAG, embeddings, vector databases, tool/function calling, structured outputs, MCP, and related technologies.
  • Develop mechanisms for agents to securely discover, access, reason over, and act upon approved enterprise data and services.
  • Prototype and rapidly evaluate emerging models, agent frameworks, and AI capabilities to determine where they can create measurable mission or engineering value.
  • Develop evaluation and testing frameworks for agent accuracy, reliability, safety, latency, cost, and task completion.
  • Implement guardrails and policy controls governing agent behavior, tool access, data access, and human approval points.
  • Integrate agentic capabilities with CI/CD and DevSecOps workflows to support repeatable development, testing, deployment, and lifecycle management.
  • Collaborate with platform engineers to operationalize AI workloads within Kubernetes/OpenShift environments.
  • Work with commercial AI and technology partners to integrate their capabilities into the broader engineering ecosystem.
  • Troubleshoot issues across models, agent frameworks, APIs, data sources, networking, identity, and infrastructure.
  • Develop reusable patterns for agent deployment, configuration, observability, evaluation, and lifecycle management.
  • Document architectures, integration patterns, agent specifications, evaluation results, and operational procedures.
  • Identify recurring AI engineering challenges that can be standardized, automated, or productized into reusable capabilities.
  • Stay current with rapidly evolving agentic AI technologies and assess their applicability to secure government environments.

Minimum Experience and Qualifications

  • Active Top Secret clearance.
  • Hands-on experience building applications or systems using large language models and generative AI.
  • Experience designing and implementing AI agents or agentic workflows.
  • Strong programming experience in Python and/or another modern programming language.
  • Experience integrating AI systems with APIs, enterprise applications, databases, and external tools.
  • Experience with one or more agent frameworks or orchestration approaches.
  • Working knowledge of RAG, embeddings, vector databases, tool/function calling, structured outputs, and prompt engineering.
  • Experience developing software in a Git-based, automated CI/CD environment.
  • Ability to rapidly prototype, test, troubleshoot, and iterate in ambiguous environments.
  • Strong understanding of software engineering fundamentals, including testing, version control, APIs, debugging, and system design.
  • Ability to work effectively alongside platform engineers, government personnel, and multiple technology vendors.

Preferred Experience and Qualifications

  • Experience with MCP (Model Context Protocol) and tool-based agent architectures.
  • Experience with multi-agent systems and agent orchestration.
  • Experience with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, NVIDIA, or comparable foundation model ecosystems.
  • Experience with NVIDIA NIM, NeMo, or similar AI inference/model-serving technologies.
  • Experience with Red Hat OpenShift AI or Kubernetes-based AI platforms.
  • Experience with agent evaluation and observability frameworks.
  • Experience implementing AI guardrails, policy enforcement, human-in-the-loop workflows, or AI safety controls.
  • Experience with LangGraph, LangChain, LlamaIndex, Semantic Kernel, or comparable frameworks.
  • Experience with RAG pipelines, vector databases, knowledge graphs, and enterprise search.
  • Experience deploying AI systems in Secret or TS/SCI environments.
  • Experience with disconnected or air-gapped AI environments.
  • Experience integrating AI into developer/DevSecOps workflows.
  • Familiarity with GitLab, Jira, Confluence, Xacta, or similar enterprise engineering and compliance tools.
  • Experience working with GPUs, model serving, inference optimization, or AI infrastructure.
  • Familiarity with UDS, Zarf, Pepr, Iron Bank, or similar secure software delivery technologies.
  • Experience taking AI prototypes into repeatable, production-ready capabilities.
  • Ability to evaluate new AI technologies quickly and make pragmatic build/buy/integrate decisions.

What Success Looks Like

  • Agentic capabilities move from prototype to mission use quickly, with working agents integrated into real government workflows rather than remaining isolated demos.
  • Agents reliably connect to approved enterprise data, tools, and services, with appropriate identity, permissions, guardrails, and human-in-the-loop controls.
  • AI capabilities are measurable and trustworthy, with repeatable evaluation methods for accuracy, reliability, task completion, security, and operational performance.
  • Reusable agent patterns emerge, reducing the engineering required to build and deploy the next agent or AI-enabled workflow.
  • AI integrates cleanly with the broader platform architecture, working effectively across the data, DevSecOps, Kubernetes/OpenShift, model, and application layers rather than creating another technology silo.
  • The engineer becomes a trusted AI technical advisor to the Mission Hero, proactively identifying where agentic technology can create mission value—and equally important, where AI is not the right solution.

Full compensation packages are based on candidate experience. Compensation ranges are established using national benchmarking data and apply across all geographic locations within the United States.

Ark bridges the gap between creating software and making it deployable. jobs.description_html:
EMPLOYER IS A CONTRACTOR FOR THE U.S. GOVERNMENT. THIS POSITION WILL REQUIRE AN ACTIVE SECRET CLEARANCE TO APPLY. 

Staff Platform Engineer

Defense Unicorns is seeking a Senior Platform Engineer to join our team. This role is responsible for designing, building, and owning the runtime production environment that bridges applications (custom development, COTS, and OSS) to the underlying platform. You will drive platform architecture decisions, set engineering standards, and serve as the technical anchor between application teams and platform teams.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You will own platform strategy and implementation end-to-end: defining technical roadmaps, solving complex problems that span multiple domains, driving cross-team delivery efficiency, and mentoring engineers across the team. We are looking for someone who builds and owns platforms, not someone who operates within infrastructure others have designed.

Key Responsibilities

  • Architect and maintain scalable runtime production environments across cloud-native and containerized systems, including transforming applications into Kubernetes-friendly formats for bare-metal deployment

jobs.title: Technical Lead/Platform Solutions Architect  (FedD236)
jobs.description_html:
Technical Lead / Platform Solution Architect

Mission Value: Serve as the technical authority across a complex, multi-vendor AI and software platform, helping the government team make sound architecture decisions, resolve cross-platform integration challenges, and establish repeatable patterns that accelerate mission delivery.

Role Description

Defense Unicorns is seeking a senior Technical Lead / Platform Solution Architect to embed with a government team and serve as the go-to technical subject matter expert across the platform architecture. This individual will connect the mission, engineering, security, data, AI, and vendor perspectives into a coherent technical approach and become a trusted technology advisor to the mission hero.

The role is intentionally hands-on and strategic. The Technical Lead will work across Kubernetes/OpenShift, GitLab and CI/CD, AI/agent infrastructure, enterprise data services, cloud infrastructure, security controls, and integration patterns. They will guide technical decisions, challenge assumptions, identify architectural risks early, and help the team move from prototype to operational capability. The ideal candidate can move fluently between executive-level mission conversations and deep technical discussions with engineers and OEM teams.

Responsibilities

Own the end-to-end technical architecture and serve as the primary technical SME across the platform ecosystem.

Become a trusted technology advisor to the mission hero, translating mission objectives into pragmatic technical choices and providing clear recommendations, tradeoffs, and risk assessments. Create and maintain the architectural “big picture” across application, platform, AI, data, networking, security, identity, and integration layers.

Lead technical integration across commercial and government technologies, including Kubernetes/OpenShift, GitLab, AI/ML services, enterprise data platforms, and supporting security tooling.Identify architectural dependencies, integration risks, bottlenecks, and technical debt early enough to prevent downstream schedule or mission impacts.

Guide engineering teams in establishing repeatable patterns for deployment, configuration, observability, identity, secrets, APIs, data access, and lifecycle management.

Work directly with OEM engineering and professional services teams to resolve cross-platform issues and ensure vendor solutions fit the overall architecture.

Evaluate emerging AI, agentic, cloud-native, and platform technologies and advise the government team on practical adoption, integration, and sequencing. Help establish technical patterns that can be reproduced across classified environments and support the transition from prototype to operational use.

Partner with the DevSecOps engineer to identify security and compliance risks early, incorporating NIST 800-53/RMF and ATO considerations into architecture and engineering decisions.

Partner with the Data Engineer and AI Agentic Engineer to ensure data, models, agents, and applications are designed to work together as an operational system.

Produce and maintain architecture diagrams, ADRs, technical standards, integration patterns, and concise decision briefs for government leadership.

Identify recurring integration and platform problems that can be standardized, automated, or productized through UDS or other reusable capabilities.

Minimum Experience and Qualifications

Active TS/SCI clearance.

Local to the National Capital Region and able to support onsite work at a government facility in Springfield, Virginia; availability for increasing onsite/SCIF interaction as the program scales.

8+ years of experience in systems engineering, platform engineering, cloud architecture, DevSecOps, or solution architecture, with demonstrated ownership of complex technical environments.

Deep hands-on understanding of Kubernetes and enterprise container platforms, preferably Red Hat OpenShift.Strong understanding of cloud infrastructure, CI/CD, Infrastructure as Code, GitOps, APIs, networking, identity, secrets, and observability.

Familiarity with NIST 800-53, RMF, ATO/C-ATO, zero-trust architecture, software supply-chain security, and continuous authorization.

Ability to understand and communicate system architecture across application, platform, AI, data, and security boundaries.

Demonstrated experience leading technical decisions in ambiguous, fast-moving environments with multiple engineering teams and technology vendors.

Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to brief senior government leaders and collaborate effectively with deeply technical engineers.

Ability to serve as a technical point of accountability without becoming a bottleneck; comfortable making informed decisions and escalating when needed.

Preferred Experience and Qualifications

Experience with AI/ML infrastructure, generative AI, agentic systems, model serving, RAG, or AI platform architecture.

Experience with Red Hat OpenShift AI, NVIDIA AI technologies, GitLab, enterprise data platforms, or comparable commercial technologies.

Experience integrating multi-vendor platforms where no single vendor owns the complete end-to-end solution.

Experience supporting Secret or TS/SCI systems and multi-domain or disconnected/air-gapped deployments.

Experience with UDS, Zarf, Pepr, Iron Bank, or similar secure software delivery and platform engineering technologies.

Experience creating architecture decision records, reference architectures, technical roadmaps, and executive-level technical briefings.

Experience advising government customers on technology strategy, modernization, platform adoption, or enterprise architecture.

Success in the Role

The government team has a single, trusted technical advisor who can connect mission goals to architecture and engineering execution. Cross-platform integration issues are identified and resolved before they become schedule or mission blockers.

Technical patterns become repeatable rather than bespoke, reducing future engineering effort as the environment expands across classifications and mission use cases.

The team can make faster, better-informed technology decisions and move from prototype to operational capability with fewer integration surprises.

jobs.title: Radar Product Manager
jobs.description_html:
Why LeoLabs? 

At LeoLabs, we’re building the living map of activity in space. Through our proprietary global radar network and AI-enabled analytics platform, we collect millions of measurements each day on more than 25,000 objects in low Earth orbit (LEO). Our radar-powered intelligence helps protect critical assets, characterize activity in orbit, monitor emerging threats, and enable safer and more effective operations for commercial and government missions. 

We’re not just building technology—we are redefining global security, safety, and transparency in space. As orbital activity accelerates and the operating environment becomes increasingly complex, LeoLabs is a trusted partner for Space Domain Awareness, Space Traffic Management, satellite operations, and national security missions around the world. 

If you're looking to work on mission-critical challenges at the intersection of aerospace, national security, sensing, software, data, and AI, your impact starts here. This position is contingent upon final approval, with an anticipated hiring timeline beginning as early as January 2027. We are beginning the search in advance of the anticipated hiring timeline. 

LeoLabs is seeking a Radar Product Manager to lead the continued development, commercialization, and growth of our transportable radar product, our radar-based space domain awareness product. 

Our transportable radar product combines advanced radar sensing, software, data processing, and operational capabilities to provide customers with persistent, high-quality information about objects and activity in low Earth orbit. Our transportable radar product extends LeoLabs' ability to deploy sensing capability where customers need it and enables a range of commercial and government missions. 

This role sits at the intersection of customers, product strategy, radar technology, engineering, operations, deployment, and business objectives. You will be responsible for understanding customer missions and market opportunities, defining where our transportable radar product should compete, shaping the capabilities and configurations customers need, and helping turn advanced radar technology into scalable products and services customers can buy, deploy, and operate. 

The ideal candidate is a strong product thinker with both commercial and technical judgment. You should have experience working in the space industry or in a closely related aerospace or national-security environment, be comfortable working with complex hardware and software systems, and be able to translate customer missions and technical capabilities into clear product and business direction. 

What You’ll Do 

  • Own the product and business strategy for our transportable radar product, including product vision, roadmap, market positioning, prioritization, packaging, configurations, and execution
  • Develop a deep understanding of our transportable radar product customers, users, missions, workflows, operational environments, procurement considerations, and buying behavior
  • Work directly with commercial and government customers, operators, mission partners, internal stakeholders, and subject-matter experts to identify unmet needs, validate product opportunities, and determine where our transportable radar product can create differentiated value
  • Identify and prioritize market segments, mission areas, use cases, deployment models, and customer problems where our transportable radar product can create meaningful mission impact and business growth
  • Translate customer, mission, and business requirements into clear product requirements, system capabilities, configurations, interfaces, and prioritized development work
  • Partner closely with radar, hardware, software, systems, data, infrastructure, and operations teams throughout the product lifecycle, from discovery and definition through development, integration, testing, deployment, operation, and iteration
  • Make product investment decisions based on customer value, strategic differentiation, revenue potential, sensor performance, technical feasibility, operational complexity, scalability, and company priorities
  • Define how our transportable radar product capabilities, configurations, service levels, and access models are packaged and positioned so customers can clearly understand what they are buying, what mission outcomes it enables, and how it differs from other LeoLabs offerings
  • Partner with Sales, Business Development, Marketing, and Customer Success to support customer engagements, technical discussions, demonstrations, proposals, strategic pursuits, pilots, and go-to-market activities
  • Help shape pricing, packaging, service models, and commercial structures for our transportable radar product offerings in partnership with Product leadership and other business stakeholders
  • Develop a strong understanding of the tradeoffs between radar performance, deployment location, coverage, capacity, tasking, reliability, availability, maintainability, cost, and customer mission outcomes
  • Partner with Engineering and Operations to understand radar performance and identify opportunities to improve sensing capability, data quality, coverage, availability, operational efficiency, and customer value
  • Help define requirements for how customers interact with and task our transportable radar product, how measurements and data products are delivered, and how our transportable radar product integrates with customer and LeoLabs software systems
  • Maintain and communicate a clear product roadmap and ensure alignment across Product, Engineering, Radar Operations, Sales, Business Development, Customer Success, and company leadership
  • Define and monitor product, business, and operational metrics that measure customer outcomes, radar performance, availability, utilization, adoption, reliability, deployment effectiveness, revenue impact, and overall product performance
  • Lead product launches and internal enablement, ensuring that customer-facing teams can effectively explain, demonstrate, position, and sell our transportable radar product capabilities
  • Continuously evaluate competing sensing solutions, emerging radar and sensor technologies, customer acquisition trends, market developments, and evolving space and national-security requirements to identify new opportunities for our transportable radar product
  • Distinguish between one-off customer requirements and repeatable market needs, ensuring our transportable radar product evolves as a scalable product family rather than a collection of bespoke radar programs
  • Help establish and improve product management practices as LeoLabs continues to scale its product organization

What We’re Looking For 

  • 5+ years of product management experience, preferably with products involving hardware, software, data, sensing, infrastructure, or other complex technical systems
  • Professional experience working in the space industry, or in a closely related aerospace, defense, or national-security environment, with demonstrated understanding of space missions, customers, operators, or technologies
  • Demonstrated experience owning products or significant product areas from market discovery and product strategy through development, deployment, launch, adoption, and iteration
  • Strong business judgment and the ability to connect product decisions to customer mission outcomes, competitive differentiation, revenue opportunities, and company strategy
  • Strong customer orientation and experience engaging directly with customers to uncover needs, validate opportunities, and translate feedback into scalable products
  • Demonstrated ability to understand complex technical systems and translate technical capabilities, limitations, and tradeoffs into clear product direction and priorities
  • Experience working across multidisciplinary engineering teams that may include hardware, software, systems, infrastructure, data, operations, or related technical functions
  • Ability to make informed prioritization decisions across competing customer requests, market opportunities, engineering constraints, operational considerations, cost, schedule, and strategic priorities
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with engineers, operators, customers, executives, and other technical and non-technical audiences
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to use technical performance data, customer feedback, market information, and business considerations to make product decisions
  • Ability to operate effectively in a fast-moving environment where customer needs, technology, operational conditions, and market requirements can evolve quickly
  • Curiosity and willingness to develop deeper expertise in radar, RF systems, space surveillance, orbital operations, and related technical domains
  • Ability to operate with a high degree of ownership and independently drive product decisions while building alignment across multiple organizations
  • Willingness and ability to travel domestically and internationally to engage directly with customers, partners, deployment teams, and internal stakeholders
  • LeoLabs is a global company with customers, radar sites, partners, and users around the world, and this role will require periodic travel to understand customer missions, support key engagements and deployments, and represent the product in-market

Preferred Qualifications 

  • Experience with radar, RF systems, remote sensing, ground-based sensors, satellite sensors, or other advanced sensing technologies
  • Experience developing or commercializing products that integrate hardware, software, data, communications, infrastructure, and operational systems
  • Direct experience with Space Domain Awareness, Space Situational Awareness, Space Surveillance and Tracking, satellite operations, orbital analysis, or related space missions
  • Familiarity with missile warning, missile tracking, and integrated air and missile defense missions, including an understanding of how sensor performance, coverage, latency, tracking quality, and data delivery support operational warning and tracking architectures
  • Experience working with satellite operators, U.S. government space organizations, allied defense organizations, intelligence organizations, or commercial space companies
  • Familiarity with radar concepts such as detection, tracking, search, revisit rates, coverage, waveforms, beam scheduling, capacity, measurement quality, or sensor tasking
  • Familiarity with orbital mechanics, tracking data, state vectors, conjunction assessment, maneuver detection, object characterization, or other space-domain concepts
  • Experience with deployed products or infrastructure where reliability, availability, maintainability, logistics, site selection, and operational support are important product considerations
  • Experience supporting government acquisition processes, strategic pursuits, proposals, demonstrations, pilots, customer evaluations, or major program captures
  • Experience defining product packaging, pricing, configurations, service levels, or go-to-market strategy for complex technical products
  • Experience working with products sold through multiple ownership, operating, or service models
  • Experience working directly with government and commercial customers in complex enterprise sales environments
  • Technical degree or background in engineering, physics, computer science, aerospace, electrical engineering, systems engineering, or a related field
  • Active U.S. Government security clearance, or the ability and willingness to obtain and maintain one, is preferred

What Success Looks Like 

In this role, success means: 

  • Our transportable radar product has a clear product and market strategy aligned with LeoLabs' broader business objectives and differentiated from competing sensing solutions
  • The organization has a strong understanding of our transportable radar product's target customers, priority missions, deployment models, use cases, value propositions, and commercial opportunities
  • Our transportable radar product capabilities and configurations are packaged and positioned in ways that customers can easily understand, evaluate, purchase, deploy, and use
  • Our transportable radar product evolves from advanced radar technology into a scalable product family that can support multiple customer missions and business models without excessive customization
  • Engineering and Operations have clear product direction, well-defined priorities, and a strong understanding of the customer and business outcomes behind the work
  • Product decisions appropriately balance mission outcomes, radar performance, customer requirements, technical feasibility, deployment complexity, cost, schedule, and business value
  • Our transportable radar product continues to improve in areas such as sensing performance, data quality, coverage, capacity, availability, reliability, deployability, operational efficiency, and customer usability
  • Customers see measurable mission value from our transportable radar product and increasingly integrate its capabilities into their operational workflows
  • Our transportable radar product contributes meaningfully to LeoLabs' revenue growth through new deployments, new customers, expansion opportunities, strategic programs, and increased adoption
  • Sales and Business Development teams have clearly defined our transportable radar product offerings, compelling demonstrations, strong positioning, and supporting materials that allow them to confidently take our transportable radar product to market
  • Product, radar, engineering, operations, and customer-facing teams remain aligned around priorities, product configurations, upcoming capabilities, deployments, and customer commitments
  • Our transportable radar product continues to evolve based on customer outcomes, operational performance, market demand, competitive dynamics, technology advances, and LeoLabs' long-term strategy

Compensation 

This position is benchmarked to Denver, CO with a base salary range of $171,000–$194,000 plus bonus and equity. Actual base salary will be determined based on the candidate’s work location, experience, skills, and other applicable factors

jobs.title: Software Product Manager
jobs.description_html:
Why LeoLabs? 

At LeoLabs, we’re building the living map of activity in space. Through our proprietary global radar network and AI-enabled analytics platform, we collect millions of measurements each day on more than 25,000 objects in low Earth orbit (LEO). Our radar-powered intelligence helps protect critical assets, characterize activity in orbit, monitor emerging threats, and enable safer and more effective operations for commercial and government missions. 

We’re not just building technology—we are redefining global security, safety, and transparency in space. As orbital activity accelerates and the operating environment becomes increasingly complex, LeoLabs is a trusted partner for Space Domain Awareness, Space Traffic Management, satellite operations, and national security missions around the world. 

If you're looking to work on mission-critical challenges at the intersection of aerospace, national security, software, data, and AI, your impact starts here. This position is contingent upon final approval, with an anticipated hiring timeline beginning as early as January 2027. We are beginning the search in advance of the anticipated hiring timeline. 

LeoLabs is seeking a Software Product Manager to join our Product organization and lead the continued development, commercialization, and growth of our SDA software product , one of LeoLabs’ core software products. 

Our SDA software product transforms LeoLabs’ radar data and space-domain information into operational intelligence, analytics, alerts, and mission workflows that help customers understand what is happening in orbit and act with greater speed and confidence. 

This role sits at the intersection of customers, market needs, product strategy, engineering, and business objectives. You will be responsible for understanding customer missions and market opportunities, defining where our SDA software product should compete, translating those needs into differentiated product capabilities, and helping turn those capabilities into products customers can adopt and buy. 

The ideal candidate is a strong product thinker with both commercial and technical judgment. You should have experience working in the space industry or in a closely related aerospace or national-security environment, be comfortable engaging directly with sophisticated commercial and government customers, and be able to translate complex mission problems into clear product and business direction. 

What You’ll Do 

  • Own the product and business strategy for our SDA software product, including product vision, roadmap, market positioning, prioritization, packaging, and execution
  • Develop a deep understanding of our SDA software product customers, users, missions, workflows, operational challenges, and buying behavior
  • Work directly with commercial and government customers, operators, analysts, internal stakeholders, and subject-matter experts to identify unmet needs, validate product opportunities, and understand where LeoLabs can create differentiated value
  • Identify and prioritize market segments, use cases, and customer problems where Our SDA software product can create meaningful mission impact and business growth
  • Translate customer, mission, and business requirements into clear product requirements, capabilities, user experiences, and prioritized development work
  • Partner closely with Engineering throughout the product lifecycle, from discovery and definition through development, testing, release, and iteration
  • Make product investment decisions based on customer value, strategic differentiation, revenue potential, technical feasibility, scalability, and company priorities
  • Define how our SDA software product capabilities are packaged and positioned so customers can clearly understand what they are buying, why it matters, and how it supports their mission
  • Partner with Sales, Business Development, Marketing, and Customer Success to support customer engagements, product demonstrations, proposals, strategic pursuits, pilots, and go-to-market activities
  • Help shape pricing, packaging, and commercial models for our SDA software product offerings in partnership with Product leadership and other business stakeholders
  • Maintain and communicate a clear product roadmap and ensure alignment across Product, Engineering, Sales, Business Development, Customer Success, Operations, and company leadership
  • Define and monitor product and business metrics that measure adoption, usage, customer outcomes, time-to-value, retention, expansion, revenue impact, and overall product performance
  • Lead product launches and internal enablement, ensuring that Sales, Customer Success, and other customer-facing teams can effectively communicate and sell new our SDA software product capabilities
  • Continuously evaluate competitors, adjacent markets, customer acquisition trends, emerging technologies, and changes in the space and national-security environment to identify new opportunities for our SDA software product
  • Distinguish between individual customer requests and repeatable market needs, ensuring our SDA software product evolves as a scalable product rather than a collection of one-off solutions
  • Help establish and improve product management practices as LeoLabs continues to scale its product organization

What We’re Looking For 

  • 5+ years of product management experience, preferably with software, data, analytics, enterprise, or other highly technical products
  • Professional experience working in the space industry, or in a closely related aerospace, defense, or national-security environment, with demonstrated understanding of space missions, customers, operators, or technologies
  • Demonstrated experience owning products or major product areas from market discovery and product strategy through development, launch, adoption, and iteration
  • Strong business judgment and the ability to connect product decisions to customer outcomes, competitive differentiation, revenue opportunities, and company strategy
  • Strong customer orientation and experience engaging directly with customers to uncover needs, validate opportunities, and translate feedback into scalable products
  • Demonstrated ability to translate complex technical, operational, or customer problems into clear product direction and priorities
  • Experience working closely with software engineering teams and technical leaders throughout the product development lifecycle
  • Ability to make informed prioritization decisions across competing customer requests, business opportunities, strategic priorities, and technical constraints
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with engineers, customers, executives, operators, and other technical and non-technical audiences
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to use both quantitative and qualitative information to make product decisions
  • Ability to operate effectively in a fast-moving environment where customer needs, technology, and market conditions can evolve quickly
  • Curiosity and willingness to develop deeper expertise in complex space, technical, and mission domains
  • Ability to operate with a high degree of ownership and independently drive product decisions while building alignment across multiple organizations
  • Willingness and ability to travel domestically and internationally to engage directly with customers, partners, and internal teams. LeoLabs is a global company with customers and users around the world, and this role will require periodic travel to understand customer missions, support key engagements, and represent the product in-market

Preferred Qualifications 

  • Experience building and commercializing products for government, aerospace, defense, intelligence, or other highly technical markets
  • Direct experience with Space Domain Awareness, Space Situational Awareness, Space Traffic Management, satellite operations, orbital analysis, command and control, or related space missions
  • Experience working with satellite operators, space mission operators, U.S. government space organizations, allied defense organizations, or commercial space companies
  • Familiarity with orbital mechanics, tracking data, conjunction assessment, maneuver detection, satellite behaviors, or other space-domain concepts
  • Experience supporting government acquisition processes, strategic pursuits, proposals, demonstrations, pilots, or customer evaluations
  • Experience working with data-intensive products, APIs, analytics platforms, event detection, visualization tools, or operational decision-support systems
  • Experience defining product packaging, pricing, positioning, or go-to-market strategy
  • Experience working directly with government and commercial customers in complex enterprise sales environments
  • Technical background or demonstrated experience working closely with highly technical engineering, data science, scientific, or aerospace teams 
  • Experience working in markets where customer requirements may be ambiguous, procurement cycles are complex, and product managers must identify common product needs across multiple customer missions
  • Active U.S. Government security clearance, or the ability and willingness to obtain and maintain one, is preferred

What Success Looks Like 

In this role, success means: 

  • Our SDA software product has a clear product and market strategy that is aligned with LeoLabs’ broader business objectives and differentiated from competing offerings
  • The organization has a strong understanding of our SDA software product ’s target customers, priority missions, use cases, value propositions, and commercial opportunities
  • Our SDA software product capabilities are packaged and positioned in ways that are easy for customers to understand, evaluate, purchase, and adopt
  • Engineering has clear product direction, well-defined priorities, and a strong understanding of the customer and business outcomes behind the work
  • Customer and market feedback consistently inform product decisions without allowing one-off customer requests to derail the broader product strategy
  • Our SDA software product delivers measurable improvements in customer mission outcomes, adoption, usage, retention, and overall customer value
  • Our SDA software product contributes meaningfully to LeoLabs’ revenue growth through new customer acquisition, expansion, strategic programs, and increased product adoption
  • Sales and Business Development teams have compelling products, demonstrations, messaging, and supporting materials that allow them to confidently take our SDA software product to market
  • Cross-functional teams have clear visibility into product priorities, upcoming capabilities, market positioning, and product launches
  • Our SDA software product continues to evolve based on customer outcomes, market demand, competitive dynamics, product data, and LeoLabs’ long-term strategy

Compensation 

This position is benchmarked to Denver, CO with a base salary range of $171,000–$194,000, plus bonus and equity. Actual base salary will be determined based on the candidate’s work location, experience, skills, and other applicable factors 

Perks and Benefits  

  • 100 USD monthly wellness benefit to support your health and well-being 
  • $300 USD home office setup stipend, available for use within your first six months 
  • $75 USD monthly home internet allowance, paid directly through your regular paycheck 
  • Individual Development Fund to support training, learning, and professional development 
  • Employee Recognition Program to celebrate contributions and achievements across the team 
  • Employee Referral Program so you can help us connect with great talent 
  • And much more! 

ITAR Requirements  

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. More information regarding ITAR can be found at DDTC’s website.

Who We Are: 

Raft (https://TeamRaft.com) is a customer-obsessed non-traditional defense tech company dedicated to empowering U.S. military and government agencies with cutting-edge AI/ML and data solutions. We are a leader in autonomous data fusion and Agentic AI, with a purposeful focus on Distributed Data Systems, Platforms at Scale, and Complex Application Development. With headquarters in McLean, VA, our range of clients includes innovative federal and public agencies leveraging design thinking, cutting-edge tech stack, and cloud-native ecosystem. We build digital solutions that impact the lives of millions of Americans.

About the Role:

As a DevOps and IT Engineering Intern at Raft, you’ll be part of a team enhancing infrastructure capabilities within RaftLabs. This role is ideal for someone passionate about DevOps and eager to build hands-on skills in Linux server administration, IT systems, and virtualization. You’ll gain valuable experience working with tools like Proxmox to support, optimize, and expand our infrastructure. Working alongside experienced engineers, you’ll contribute to configuring Linux environments, automating processes, and building secure, scalable systems.

What we are looking for:

  • Passion for DevOps, IT infrastructure, and system optimization.
  • Basic knowledge of Linux operating systems and a willingness to learn server administration.
  • Interest in virtualization tools, like Proxmox, for managing and optimizing server environments.
  • Understanding of version control tools, such as Git, for collaborative development.
  • Ability to work with team members to enhance feature capabilities and infrastructure in RaftLabs.
  • Analytical mindset and eagerness to solve problems and improve system performance.
  • Currently enrolled in an IT, Computer Science, Engineering, or related degree program.
  • U.S. citizenship is required due to potential exposure to sensitive government-related work.

Highly Preferred:

  • Exposure to scripting languages (e.g., Bash, Python) and an interest in learning automation techniques.
  • Familiarity with Agile project methodologies or a desire to work in a fast-paced, collaborative setting.
  • Strong communication skills to effectively share technical insights within the team.
  • Curiosity and drive to stay updated on DevOps tools, trends, and best practices.

Work Type:

  • Location: Onsite at Raft HQ in McLean, VA
  • Duration: June to August 2027
  • Hours: Part-time, up to 40 hours per week
  • Compensation: $20 - $24 per hour, based on experience and qualifications.

Our Vision Statement:  

We bridge the gap between humans and data through radical transparency and our obsession with the mission. 

Our Customer Obsession: 

We will approach every deliverable like it's a product. We will adopt a customer-obsessed mentality. As we grow, and our footprint becomes larger, teams and employees will treat each other not only as teammates but customers. We must live the customer-obsessed mindset, always. This will help us scale and it will translate to the interactions that our Rafters have with their clients and other product teams that they integrate with. Our culture will enable our success and set us apart from other companies.

How do we get there? 

Public-sector modernization is critical for us to live in a better world. We, at Raft, want to innovate and solve complex problems. And, if we are successful, our generation and the ones that follow us will live in a delightful, efficient, and accessible world where out-of-box thinking, and collaboration is a norm. 

Raft’s core philosophy is Ubuntu: I Am, Because We are. We support our “nadi” by elevating the other Rafters. We work as a hyper collaborative team where each team member brings a unique perspective, adding value that did not exist before. People make Raft special. We celebrate each other and our cognitive and cultural diversity. We are devoted to our practice of innovation and collaboration. 

We’re an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran or disability status.

jobs.title: AI Software Engineer
jobs.description_html:
AI Software Engineer

Second Front Systems is looking for an ambitious, mission-focused, full-stack AI Software Engineer to strengthen our growing Research and Development organization building AI-native platform capabilities.

Operating at the intersection of AI systems engineering and national security infrastructure, you will be responsible for designing, building, and shipping production agentic AI systems while establishing the cloud infrastructure and governance they operate within.

You will move from prototype to production across agent design, implementation, LLM integration, and cloud deployment, ensuring measurable output quality and user authorization at every stage, ensuring that Game Warden and downstream products integrate AI as foundational capability rather than feature. Your solutions will include evaluative rigor and organizational fluency.

We need someone capable of building and shipping agentic systems with LangGraph, LangChain, tool-calling, and multi-step orchestration; operating cloud infrastructure (EKS, Terraform, Helm) and LLM gateway patterns across AWS Bedrock, Anthropic, OpenAI, Cohere, self-hosted models and provider-agnostic architectures; and defining and measuring agent quality through evaluation suites, then translating results into model selection and architecture decisions.

As a key partner to our Product and Engineering teams, which are seeking to identify and deploy AI workflows across onboarding, deployment, monitoring, and remediation, you will advise on agent architecture and scope, model selection, implementation, and responsible AI governance. You will build documentation and reusable components that multiply organizational AI capability, serving as technical authority translating research-grade AI systems into mission-ready product.

Note: Candidates must reside in one of our approved hiring hubs:
• DC/Maryland/Virginia
• Denver/Colorado Springs, CO

This is a full-time position.

What You'll Do
• Architect production agentic AI systems using LangGraph and LangChain with focus on reliability, traceability, and measurable output quality.
• Build agent components including ingestion pipelines, embedding strategies, chunking, retrieval, and re-ranking, and tool suites across managed knowledge-base services, vector databases, and internal and external APIs.
• Connect agents to corporate tools and knowledge through Model Context Protocol, constructing both MCP servers and consuming clients.
• Establish and operate cloud infrastructure for R&D AI systems: Amazon EKS, Terraform, Helm, and GitOps delivery patterns.
• Measure agent and LLM output quality through evaluation and regression suites covering groundedness, faithfulness, relevance, and retrieval quality, running in CI.
• Partner with Product teams to scope high-leverage AI opportunities across workflows and advise on agent design, model selection and output quality standards.

What You Bring
• 2+ years full-time software, ML, or AI engineering experience with hands-on production work building and shipping LLM-based systems.
• Hands-on experience building agentic AI systems with tool-calling agents and multi-step orchestration using LangGraph, LangChain, or equivalent.
• Production experience with Retrieval-Augmented Generation including vector stores, embedding models, chunking strategies, and retrieval quality optimization.
• Experience deploying containerized AI services to cloud environments using Docker, Kubernetes (EKS preferred), and infrastructure as code (Terraform preferred).
• Demonstrated ability to communicate AI concepts and recommendations to non-technical stakeholders and cross-functional teams.

  • U.S. citizenship required!


    Preferred
    • Experience building MCP servers or clients, or integrating agents with enterprise tools and knowledge bases.
    • Experience with AWS AI services such as Bedrock Knowledge Bases, AgentCore, and OpenSearch.
    • Experience operating LLM gateways or serving infrastructure (e.g., LiteLLM, vLLM, GPU-backed self-hosted models), including single- and multi-tenant designs.
    • Experience driving AI adoption across a product organization: not just building, but enabling others to use AI effectively.
    • Experience working in or with the Department of Defense, federal agencies, or regulated environments, and familiarity with compliance frameworks such as NIST 800-53, FedRAMP, or NATO D32.

The base salary for this position will fall between $130,000 and $160,000. Your ultimate compensation will be determined by professional background, technical proficiency, seniority, and regional cost factors. Furthermore, this opportunity includes potential eligibility for equity awards and discretionary bonuses, rounding out a comprehensive total rewards offering.

Success at 2F Looks Like:
• A proactive and solutions oriented mindset
• Viewing obstacles as opportunities for growth
• Having a bias toward action and tangible, measurable results
• Being team-oriented with a focus on personal responsibility and autonomy

Perks & Benefits:
This role is a full time position. As a public benefit corporation, we’re a team of purpose-driven trailblazers transforming the future of U.S. national security. We hire the best to do their best and, as such, we are committed to providing the perks and benefits you need to be successful—both in- and outside the workplace.

We eliminate the friction that slows innovation, enabling faster, more secure development and deployment of software across government and regulated networks. Built by national security veterans and backed by top-tier venture capital, our platform is trusted by the world’s leading organizations to cut deployment timelines from years to weeks. We move fast, solve hard problems, and deliver trusted capabilities where they’re needed most. jobs.title: Commercial Sales Account Executive
jobs.description_html:
Second Front Systems (2F) is seeking a Commercial Sales Account Executive to drive new business for 2F Game Warden, our authorized DevSecOps platform that enables the authorization and deployment of software onto government and defense networks fast. This is a full-cycle, quota-carrying sales seat on a growing commercial team, and we don't want someone who's looking to coast on inbound.

Your north star is new logos and closed-won revenue. You own the full sales cycle for 2F Game Warden—from first conversation to signed contract—and you're judged on quota attainment, not activity.

This person must also be passionate about the 2F mission. Every deal you close puts a software company's technology in front of warfighters and mission owners faster—cutting deployment timelines from years to weeks. We want someone who closes business and understands why it matters.

You'll prospect, pitch, and close independent software vendors (ISVs) and technology companies who need a fast, credible path to DoW and FedRAMP authorization/certification. Compliance sales is a sea of sameness—generic RFPs, slow legal cycles, buyers who've been burned before. We want you to be the rep who makes 2F Game Warden the obvious choice and gets the deal signed.

This is a hunter's and a closer's role for an experienced seller. You bring proven hunter skills, a track record of closed-won revenue, pipeline hygiene and discipline, and the instinct for navigating technical and procurement stakeholders—and you'll have the autonomy to run your territory like a business, with minimal oversight from leadership. You'll also be looked to as an informal mentor for less experienced reps and as a voice in shaping how the commercial sales team sells.

Note: Candidates must reside in one of our approved hiring hubs

  • DC/Maryland/Virginia

  • Denver/Colorado Springs, CO

What You'll Do

  • Own and prioritize a complex book of business selling 2F Game Warden to independent software vendors (ISVs) and technology companies pursuing DoW, IC, and federal civilian markets—allocating your time and resources across accounts to hit team objectives.
