jobs.title: Key Account Director, Small Cities (East)
jobs.description_html:
Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors to first responders, soldiers in battlefield scenarios, and beyond.

About the Team: Public safety is where drone technology faces the highest stakes. Agencies across the country are standing up Drone as First Responder (DFR) programs that put an aircraft over an emergency within seconds of a call. As drone programs move from the age of tools to the age of infrastructure, we are expanding our public safety sales team to meet that demand.

About the role: As a Key Account Director, Small City at Skydio, you will lead a regional team of Key Account Leaders selling into our highest-volume public safety segment, agencies with 1 to 40 sworn personnel. This is a first-line leadership role, and the job comes down to three things: recruiting the right people, coaching them into great sellers, and keeping them here.

You will not carry your own accounts. Your number is your team's number, and you will hit it by making each person on the team better: sharpening deal strategy, getting into the field on their most competitive pursuits, and building the territory, pipeline, and forecast discipline that makes a region predictable. You will work alongside peer Directors leading other segments and geographies, and across Channel, Sales Engineering, Business Development, Marketing, Strategic Relationships, Government Relations, and Mission Success.

What makes this segment distinct is scale. Your team works through many opportunities every quarter, so you will lead through the funnel as much as through individual deals. Conversion rates, cycle time, stage velocity, and activity quality will tell you where to intervene long before any single deal review would. You also own the region's upmarket radar: some small-city agencies are the leading edge of something much larger, and your team needs to spot them early and route them into the right motion alongside our Mid-City and T1200 teams.

You will also set the standard for how the team works, not only what it sells. We sell autonomous flying robots and the artificial intelligence that powers them. Every seller here uses AI tools as a normal part of running a territory, and you will model that, coach to it, and hire for it.

This is a highly competitive market, and much of the work happens alongside our channel. Your team will sell against incumbent platforms and well-funded challengers, and you will set the standard for how they win.

Location: Remote, Eastern U.S. territory (AL, AR, CT, DC, DE, FL, GA, IN, KY, LA, MA, MD, ME, MI, MS, NC, NH, NJ, NY, OH, OK, PA, PR, RI, SC, TN, VA, VT, WV)

How we work

These are the standards we hire to, and as a leader you own them for your region. You set the bar in who you hire, what you coach to, and what you tolerate.

  • High integrity. Public safety is a tight-knit community. Chiefs and Sheriffs talk to each other, and a reputation for straight answers travels fast. We sell what the ecosystem is actually capable of, we are clear about where the product is today and where it's headed, and we win on our own merits. There's no compromise here.

  • Sales is a team sport. One team. No lone wolves. Deals are won by account leaders, sales engineering, business development, channel, marketing, strategic relationships, government relations, and mission success pulling in the same direction, and our partners are part of that team, not a channel to be managed around. The best people here care more about the collective number than their own slice of it.

  • Great conversationalists. This is the craft of the job: asking better questions than anyone else in the room, listening for what a chief or sheriff isn't saying, real curiosity about how an agency operates. Not polish, not a rehearsed pitch. Trust in this market is built one honest conversation at a time, and it is the thing competitors cannot copy.

  • Curious, and fluent with the tools. Everyone on this team uses AI as a normal part of their work: researching agencies, preparing for meetings, analyzing pipeline, drafting and then editing. That takes taste more than technical skill: knowing what a quality result looks like, describing a problem precisely enough to get it, and catching the tool when it is confidently wrong. The same muscle makes a great seller. Discovery is specifying the problem; qualification is checking the output. We hire people who are curious about how things work, whether that's an agency's budget, a council's politics, or the aircraft's autonomy, and who have spent the last two years embracing AI rather than waiting to be told to use it.

How you'll make an impact

Recruit

  • Own hiring for your region: build a continuous talent pipeline, run a fast and rigorous process, and personally close the candidates you want

  • Hire to the bar above: integrity, team instinct, conversational craft, and fluency with the tools matter as much as a closed-won history

  • Screen for evidence, not adjectives: attainment stated year by year with the misses included, deal stories with the mechanics of how the customer bought, and something the candidate has built or changed in how they work in the last two years

  • Run a structured process: the same core questions for every candidate, a live working session, independent scoring, and a debrief that decides on evidence

  • Onboard and ramp new Key Account Leaders with a clear path from first day to first award, and hold the ramp accountable

Coach

  • Run 1:1s and deal reviews that build judgment rather than just inspect pipeline

  • Get in the field: join demos, customer meetings, and executive conversations, then debrief with specific, usable feedback

  • Coach the competitive game: POV strategy, shaping requirements early, framing Skydio's unique differentiators, displacement plays, and defending accounts under attack

  • Build MEDDPICC rigor, channel fluency, and forecast honesty into how the team works, not just what they report

  • Raise the team's fluency with AI tools: build shared workflows for customer research, call prep, RFP response, and pipeline analysis, and hold the line that nothing AI-drafted reaches a customer unreviewed

Retain

  • Build a team that people don't want to leave: clear expectations, real development paths, and recognition that lands

  • Own territory and quota design so assignments are achievable, equitable, and worth staying for

  • Have honest career conversations early, address disengagement before it becomes a resignation, and be the escalation path your team trusts to clear obstacles

Run the region

  • Own the region number: pipeline coverage, forecast accuracy, linearity across the quarter, and the analysis behind them

  • Partner with Channel on partner strategy, joint planning, and the deal structures that get customers to yes

  • Act as executive sponsor on your team's largest and most competitive pursuits: present in the room, without taking the deal over

  • Represent your region's customer insight, competitive intelligence, and product gaps to Marketing and Product

  • Work with Channel on where partners extend reach, where direct is the right path, and how the two stay coordinated

  • Partner with Mid-City and T1200 leaders on clean routing, shared credit, and a smooth customer experience when an account graduates

What makes you a good fit

Required

  • 2+ years leading quota-carrying sellers as a first-line manager, with team attainment you can state year by year, including the year you missed and what you changed

  • 4+ years total in enterprise software, hardware, or SaaS sales, including personal success closing complex, multi-stakeholder deals

  • Demonstrated success recruiting sellers: a real network, a clear point of view on what good looks like, a structured process you can describe, and the ability to close candidates

  • A coaching approach you can articulate, with specific examples of people who got measurably better working for you

  • Strong voluntary retention history, a record of developing people into larger roles, and the judgment to move quickly when someone isn't right for the seat

  • Experience selling or leading teams into SLED customers, with working knowledge of procurement vehicles and budget and grant cycles

  • Fluency selling with and through channel partners

  • Daily, systematic use of AI tools in your own work, and at least one workflow, analysis, or tool you built or changed in the last two years that made you or your team measurably better (we will ask you to show it, not describe it)

  • Executive presence with both customer leadership and your own team, and high personal integrity under quota pressure

  • Ability to travel at least 50% of the time, and based in East Region

  • Personal success in a high-velocity, high-volume selling environment

  • Data-fluent coaching: you manage a funnel by its metrics and can point to the specific lever behind a rep's result

  • Experience building or maintaining a repeatable sales process that holds up as volume and headcount grow

  • Obtaining FAA Part 107 certification within the first 60 days of employment is strongly encouraged for all Skydio employees and required for certain positions.

Preferred

  • Experience in public safety, specifically law enforcement, fire, or emergency management; experience standing up or scaling a high-volume segment

  • Experience building a team from a small base rather than inheriting a mature one

  • You have built something with AI that other people use, whether a research tool, an analysis, or a team workflow, and you can talk about what the first version got wrong

  • Curiosity that shows: you can explain how something outside sales works (an agency budget, an airspace waiver, the aircraft's autonomy) in plain language, and you learn fast

  • Familiarity with MEDDPICC, Salesforce, Clari, BGov, GovWin, Slack, and Google Workspace

  • UAV, robotics, or emerging technology background, and comfort in a fast-moving environment

What to expect from our process

We run a structured process and we tell you what it is. A 30-minute conversation with the hiring manager. A deep dive on your leadership record: hiring, coaching, retention, and the team number, year by year. A working session where you use your own AI tools on a realistic problem from this region and walk us through your choices. A panel on the public safety market and how you would run the region. A conversation about how you think. References with people who worked for you and with you. Every interviewer scores independently against the same rubric before we compare notes.

On AI in the process: draft your resume yourself and refine it with AI if you like; we want your real experience, well expressed. Use whatever tools you want to prepare. Expect to use them in the working session. Leave them off during the conversational interviews so we can see how you think in real time. We use AI to draft job descriptions like this one and to take notes, and a human makes every hiring decision.

Compensation: At Skydio, our compensation packages for regular, full-time employees include competitive base salaries, equity in the form of stock options, and comprehensive benefits packages. Compensation will vary based on factors, including skill level, proficiencies, transferable knowledge, and experience. Relocation assistance may also be provided for eligible roles. The annual base salary range for this position is $144,000 - $180,000 + commission*. Fundamentally, we believe that equity is the key to long-term financial growth, and we ensure all regular, full-time employees have the opportunity to significantly benefit from the company's success. Regular, full-time employees are eligible to enroll in the Company’s group health insurance plans. Regular, full-time employees are eligible to receive the following benefits: Paid vacation time, sick leave, holiday pay and 401K savings plan. This position and all associated benefits are subject to applicable federal, state, and local laws, as well as the Company’s policies and eligibility criteria.

*Compensation for certain positions may vary based on the position’s location.

jobs.title: Sales Director, Emerging Markets
jobs.description_html:
Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors to first responders, soldiers in battlefield scenarios, and beyond.

About the Team

Emerging Markets is where Skydio finds its next big industries. The team sells into manufacturing, architecture, engineering and construction, oil and gas, telecom and digital infrastructure, mining, agriculture, and waste. These are thousands of large enterprises running sprawling physical sites, and many of them score as strong fits for autonomous docks. Skydio has already landed some of the largest drone programs in these industries. The opportunity now is to turn those wins into repeatable plays, industry by industry.

About the role

Sales Director, Emerging Markets, you will build and lead the team: four Account Executives on the largest enterprises, two of them new seats you will hire, including a dedicated Energy Sector role. Two BDRs support the team on net-new land deals. You will be in the seat before your new sellers, so you will shape the team, the territories, and the playbook from the start. This business is planned to nearly double next year and keep growing quickly as the team scales.

This role keeps the development mandate for Commercial Sales. You will work out which industries and use cases are ready for docks, prove them with flagship customers, and hand the team a repeatable motion. The best deals here stack use cases on one site: asset inspection, progress monitoring, EHS, emergency response, and security. Your team will find the first use case, land it, and expand from there. When an industry is ready to stand on its own, it graduates into its own team, the way Site Security did this year. Oil and gas is next.

You will work alongside peer leaders in Utilities and Site Security, and closely with Solutions Engineering, Partnerships, Customer Success, Deployment, Product, and Marketing. We sell autonomous flying robots and the AI that powers them, and every seller here uses AI tools as a normal part of running a territory. You will model that, coach to it, and hire for it.

Location: Remote, US

How we work

High integrity. Industrial buyers are practical and skeptical, and a reputation for straight answers travels fast. We sell what the product can do today, we are clear about where it's headed, and we win on our own merits.

Sales is a team sport. No lone wolves. Enterprise programs are won by account leaders, solutions engineering, partners, customer success, and deployment pulling in the same direction. The best people here care more about the collective number than their own slice of it.

Great conversationalists. Ask better questions than anyone else in the room. Listen for what a plant manager or an EHS director isn't saying. Be curious about how a refinery, a factory, or a jobsite actually runs. Trust is built one honest conversation at a time.

Curious, and fluent with the tools. Everyone on this team uses AI to research accounts, prepare for meetings, analyze pipeline, and draft and then edit. That takes judgment more than technical skill: knowing what a good result looks like and catching the tool when it is confidently wrong.

How you'll make an impact

Recruit

  • Hire the two new Account Executives, including a dedicated Energy Sector role, and build a continuous talent pipeline as the team grows

  • Run a fast and rigorous process and personally close the candidates you want

  • Hire for integrity, team instinct, conversational skill, and fluency with the tools as much as for a closed-won history

  • Onboard and ramp new sellers so they start with a book, relationships, and identified opportunities, not an empty list

Coach

  • Run 1:1s and deal reviews that build judgment, not just inspect pipeline

  • Get in the field: join executive meetings, site walks, and pilot reviews, then give specific, usable feedback

  • Coach the industrial enterprise sale: finding the operational pain, proving value in a pilot, and turning one site into a multi-site program

  • Coach use case stacking: expanding from the first use case into inspection, EHS, progress monitoring, and security on the same docks

  • Build MEDDPICC rigor and forecast honesty into how the team works: current close dates, current notes, no duplicate or stale opportunities

  • Raise the team's fluency with AI: shared workflows for account research, call prep, RFP response, and pipeline analysis, with nothing AI-drafted reaching a customer unreviewed

Retain

  • Build a team people don't want to leave: clear expectations, real development paths, and recognition that lands

  • Design territories and quotas that are achievable, fair, and worth staying for

  • Have honest career conversations early, and be the escalation path your team trusts to clear obstacles

Run the Emerging Markets business

  • Own the Emerging number: pipeline coverage, forecast accuracy, linearity, and the analysis behind them, presented to executive leadership every month

  • Decide where the team plays: use account scoring and win data to focus on the industries where docks fit best, starting with oil and gas, AEC, and manufacturing

  • Build industry playbooks from flagship wins so every new seller can repeat them

  • Route accounts cleanly: hand site security pursuits to the Security team and smaller companies to Inside Sales, and work with Partnerships where a partner extends reach

  • Act as executive sponsor on the team's largest pursuits, present in the room without taking the deal over

  • Bring customer insight, competitive intelligence, and product gaps back to Product and Marketing

What makes you a good fit

Required

  • 2+ years leading quota-carrying enterprise sellers as a first-line manager, with team attainment you can state year by year, including the year you missed and what you changed

  • 7+ years in enterprise sales of hardware, software, or SaaS, with personal success closing complex, multi-site deals with large industrial enterprises

  • Experience selling into industrial markets such as oil and gas, manufacturing, AEC, mining, or telecom, to operations, asset management, EHS, or engineering leaders

  • A record of opening new markets or verticals: finding the first customers, proving the use case, and building a repeatable play

  • Experience building a team from a small base, including hiring the first sellers

  • A coaching approach you can describe, with specific examples of people who got measurably better working for you

  • Strong retention history and a record of developing people into larger roles

  • Daily use of AI tools in your own work, and at least one workflow, analysis, or tool you built or changed in the last two years that made you or your team measurably better (we will ask you to show it)

  • Executive presence with customer leadership and with your own team, and high personal integrity under quota pressure

  • Ability to travel at least 50% of the time

Preferred

  • Background in UAS, robotics, industrial IoT, inspection technology, or other emerging technology

  • Operations, engineering, or EHS experience in an industrial setting

  • Relationships across oil and gas, manufacturing, or AEC

  • Fluency selling with and through channel partners

  • Familiarity with MEDDPICC, Salesforce, Clari, Slack, and Google Workspace

  • Curiosity that shows: you can explain how something outside sales works (a refinery turnaround, a construction progress report, the aircraft's autonomy) in plain language

What to expect from our process

We run a structured process and tell you what it is. A conversation with the hiring manager. A deep dive on your leadership record: hiring, coaching, retention, and the team number, year by year. A working session where you use your own AI tools on a realistic industrial account problem and walk us through your choices. A panel on the market and how you would build this team. References with people who worked for you and with you. Every interviewer scores independently against the same rubric before we compare notes.

Draft your resume yourself and refine it with AI if you like. Use whatever tools you want to prepare, and expect to use them in the working session. Leave them off during conversational interviews so we can see how you think in real time. A human makes every hiring decision.

Physical Site Security is transforming at a rapid pace. Historically guards have been the primary force behind Site Security. Today, the largest enterprises in the country are looking towards deployment of technology, robotics, and AI to augment and improve their security posture. Many are now putting Skydio Docks over their fulfillment centers, data centers, distribution hubs, and campuses to patrol perimeters, respond to alarms, and put eyes on an incident in seconds. Security is the fastest-growing part of Skydio's commercial business and is now a standalone team. Our largest site security customers include some of the biggest names in retail, logistics, and technology, and the account base behind them is thousands of companies wide.

As Sales Director, Site Security, you will lead nine quota-carrying sellers: six Strategic Account Managers on the largest enterprises and three Enterprise Account Executives on the next tier. Five of the nine are new seats you will hire. Each seller is paired with Solutions Engineering, and three dedicated BDRs that build net-new pipeline for the team. This team carries the largest number in Commercial Sales and is planned to grow several-fold over the next three years.

This is a build, not a harvest. The team works a book of thousands of large enterprises where only a small fraction are customers today. Your job is to turn a handful of flagship wins into a repeatable motion: one team, one playbook, every facility type. A perimeter is a perimeter. A win at a data center should teach the team how to win at a distribution center, a hospital, or a stadium. One rep owns each logo, and we never put two account teams on one account.

Much of this market is already held by the contract security firms that staff guard posts at these sites. They own the relationships, the master contracts, and the budget line. We grow with them, not around them. You will make sure your team sells with these partners, and that the rep who owns the account gets credit when a partner carries the deal.

You will work alongside peer leaders in Utilities and Emerging markets, and closely with Strategic Partnerships, Solutions Engineering, Customer Success, Deployment, Product, and Marketing. We sell autonomous flying robots and the AI that powers them, and every seller here uses AI tools as a normal part of running a territory. You will model that, coach to it, and hire for it.

How we work

High integrity. Security leaders talk to each other, and a reputation for straight answers travels fast. We sell what the product can do today, including uptime, SLAs, and how much of the operation is autonomous, we are clear about where it's headed, and we win on our own merits.

Sales is a team sport. No lone wolves. Site security programs are won by account leaders, solutions engineering, partnerships, contract security firms, customer success, and deployment pulling in the same direction. The best people here care more about the collective number than their own slice of it.

Great conversationalists. Ask better questions than anyone else in the room. Listen for what a Chief Security Officer isn't saying. This role leads the readiness function for the weastern half of the dock business, owning the customer journey from pre-sales readiness — technical, policy, and operational — through deployment, training, and go-live, and it is measured on the team's outcomes rather than your own: on-time deployments, smooth launches, and confident customers.

This role reports to the Director, Launch Team.

About the Team:

The Launch Team is the operational arm of Skydio's dock business. We sit between the opportunity and the running program, and readiness means everything an agency needs to launch: the site, the policy and public approval behind it, the flight operation that will run it, and a clean handoff to Customer Success. We do not perform every piece of that work, but we project manage the customer to all of it and are accountable for the date.

The team is measured on time-to-launch, readiness gate adherence, deployment schedule performance, and the condition of the program at handoff. Readiness capacity is sized against dock site volume, so the function has to scale faster than headcount.

Readiness Specialists are critical members of the Skydio organization and work closely with Solutions Engineers, Deployment Engineering, Legal and Policy, and Customer Success to support successful deployments and the long-term success of Public Safety sUAS programs

Lead the team

  • Identify patterns and recurring blockers across launches and drive systemic fixes rather than one-off workarounds, so the function scales against dock volume rather than headcount.

  • 5+ years of federal government or defense experience in a discipline relevant to UAS — operations, maintenance, ISR, test and evaluation, acquisition, or training.

  • 1+ years leading a technical team, formally or as a technical lead with hiring and mentorship responsibility. First-time managers with a demonstrated record of leading and developing people in an operational environment will be considered.

  • Demonstrated understanding of a defense acquisition process for technology, from requirements development through evaluation, award, and fielding.

  • Technical depth in at least one core area: UAS platforms, RF and datalink systems, EO/IR and other sensor payloads, software integration and APIs, cloud and data architecture, or government IT security.

  • Comfort operating inside a Sales organization, including owning a quota, deal strategy, and the judgment to know when to commit technical resources and when to decline.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication. You can brief an operator, a program manager, and a general officer without changing the facts.

  • Lead by example. Willing to do whatever is needed to get a customer situation resolved.

Nice to Have

  • Direct experience supporting SOCOM or its components (NSWC, MARSOC, AFSOC, USASOC, JSOC), a Theater Special Operations Command, or Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force or Space Force units.

  • Prior military UAS operator, maintainer, or instructor certification.

  • Experience with shipboard, small boat, or maritime UAS employment, including launch and recovery from a moving deck.

  • Hands-on experience with MANET radios and secure comms (TSM, TrellisWare, Silvus, Persistent Systems), and familiarity with counter-UAS and airspace deconfliction.

jobs.location: Hub - San Francisco; Hybrid - San Francisco, CA; Hybrid - Seattle, WA; New York - Remote
jobs.description_html:
Why Socure?

Socure is building the identity trust infrastructure for the digital economy — verifying 100% of good identities in real time and stopping fraud before it starts. The mission is big, the problems are complex, and the impact is felt by businesses, governments, and millions of people every day.

We hire people who want that level of responsibility. People who move fast, think critically, act like owners, and care deeply about solving customer problems with precision. If you want predictability or narrow scope, this won’t be your place. If you want to help build the future of identity with a team that holds a high bar for itself — keep reading.

Socure’s mission is to verify 100% of good identities while eliminating fraud online. With RiskOS, we are expanding that mission into an AI-powered operating system for fraud, risk, identity, and compliance operations - serving some of the world’s largest financial institutions, government agencies, prediction markets, gaming companies, marketplaces, fintechs, and digital platforms.

 

As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you will help move AI-assisted workflows from promising ideas to trusted production systems. You will work directly with large strategic customers and partners, own the path from discovery and technical scoping to system design, build, deployment, evaluation, and adoption, and solve problems where speed, trust, explainability, and control all matter.

 

This is not a traditional implementation, advisory, or professional services role. You will be an embedded builder: close enough to customer teams to understand how work actually happens, technical enough to build into real environments, and product-minded enough to turn what works into reusable RiskOS capabilities.

What you will do

  • Build with strategic customers and partners. Work side by side with large enterprises, public sector organizations, marketplaces, gaming platforms, fintechs, and other high-scale digital businesses to understand their workflows, data environments, technical constraints, business goals, and operational pain points.

  • Own deployments from prototype to production. Lead discovery, technical scoping, solution design, build, integration, testing, rollout, and adoption for AI-assisted RiskOS workflows in real customer environments.

  • Turn complex operations into working systems. Translate customer policies, SOPs, data sources, and operational processes into RiskOS workflows, integrations, data mappings, tool connections, case flows, and agent behaviors that can operate reliably in production.

  • Build the connective tissue. Write code, configure systems, debug issues, and integrate with customer infrastructure, APIs, data sources, security boundaries, analyst tools, and operational systems when progress depends on it.

 

  • Evaluate and improve agentic workflows. Help define how agents interact with tools, data, evidence, decisions, analyst queues, and business logic, then tune those workflows through testing, evals, observability, guardrails, feedback, and production learnings.

  • Prove measurable customer value. Measure whether deployed workflows improve speed, accuracy, consistency, analyst productivity, review burden, evidence quality, operational control, or other customer-defined outcomes.

  • Turn field learning into platform leverage. Surface product gaps, implementation friction, and repeatable patterns, then partner with product, engineering, data science, security, and GTM teams to convert them into reusable templates, playbooks, primitives, and product capabilities.

What you bring

  • Strong hands-on technical ability. You have experience building practical solutions across APIs, integrations, workflow logic, data mappings, internal tools, scripts, production systems, cloud services, or similar technical surfaces.

  • End-to-end ownership. You can take an ambiguous customer problem from discovery to production, making good tradeoffs across scope, speed, quality, risk, and long-term platform leverage.

  • Customer-facing problem solving. You have worked directly with enterprise customers, strategic partners, or internal business stakeholders to understand messy problems, define workable solutions, and ship usable outcomes.

  • Product-minded engineering judgment. You can move fluidly between architecture, implementation, debugging, user needs, product tradeoffs, operational risk, and stakeholder communication.

  • Systems thinking and calm execution. You can break complex workflows into modular, testable, improvable components, spot risks early, and keep teams moving with clarity and follow-through.

  • High agency and comfort with ambiguity. You thrive in fast-moving environments where requirements are incomplete, priorities evolve, and the category is still being defined.

  • Relevant technical background. You likely have 4+ years of experience in software engineering, forward deployed engineering, solutions engineering, implementation engineering, applied AI engineering, technical consulting, or a similarly hands-on technical role. Experience with Python, SQL, APIs, cloud services, workflow tools, LLM workflows, retrieval systems, tool calling, copilots, evaluation frameworks, observability, or agentic systems is especially helpful.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience deploying AI, ML, LLM, or decision-support systems in production environments.

  • Experience in fraud, risk, identity verification, KYC, KYB, AML, sanctions, adverse media, transaction monitoring, disputes, trust and safety, or compliance operations.

  • Experience working with large financial institutions, government agencies, marketplaces, gaming companies, fintechs, or other complex enterprise customers.

  • Experience with workflow orchestration, case management, rules engines, decisioning platforms, operational automation, evaluation pipelines, or customer-specific implementation tooling.

What success looks like in year one

  • Large strategic customers and partners are live or in advanced rollout with AI-assisted RiskOS workflows that solve meaningful operational problems.

  • Deployed workflows show measurable customer value, such as faster investigations, lower manual review burden, better evidence quality, stronger consistency, improved operational control, or higher analyst productivity.

  • Customer-specific lessons have been converted into reusable templates, playbooks, evaluation patterns, workflow primitives, implementation accelerators, or product requirements.

  • Product and engineering teams have a sharper roadmap based on real deployment learnings, not abstract requirements.

  • Socure has a clearer repeatable motion for deploying agentic workflows across fraud, risk, identity, and compliance operations.

jobs.description_html:

Senior Product Manager, Identity Products

About the role

We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to build and take to market a new category of products at Socure: proactive identity notifications. These are subscription products that continuously monitor identities on our customers' behalf and push an alert when something material about that identity changes.

This is a zero-to-one role with a near-term launch. You will own the first product in this line end to end: defining what good looks like, closing any performance gaps that stand between us and a product customers will pay for, shaping the event contract and subscription model, and running it from beta through GA. More event types will follow close behind, and the scope will continue to expand as the portfolio grows.

Data is the heart of this role. The quality of a proactive notification product is the quality of the data underneath it: how much of the real world it sees, how accurate it is, and how quickly it knows. You will own that. You will establish the performance metrics that define success, decide what we need to source and what a candidate source has to prove, and make the call on which sources have earned their place and which have not. A dedicated Data Partnerships team runs discovery, negotiation, licensing, and vendor management against the brief you set, alongside data science and engineering.

You will also own commercialization. Pricing and packaging, commercial terms, early-adopter recruitment, beta and GA phasing, enablement, and coordinating every function to a launch date all sit with you.

This is a highly technical and highly commercial role. It suits a PM who is equally comfortable arguing about precision and recall methodology with a data scientist in the morning and defending a pricing model to the executive team in the afternoon.

What you'll do

Product definition and launch

  • Own the roadmap, definition, and launch of proactive identity notification products, from first beta customer through general availability.

  • Define the customer-facing event contract: what the notification contains, its lifecycle semantics, and how customers consume and act on it.

  • Design a systematic customer feedback loop so every notification we send makes the next one better.

  • Begin the product definition for the next event types on the roadmap, where the customer problem is more open-ended and the framing work is still to be done.

Data source strategy

  • Own what we source and why: define the gaps in our coverage, specify what a candidate source must prove, and set the bar it has to clear. Data Partnerships runs discovery and commercial negotiation against that brief.

  • Run rigorous, hypothesis-driven evaluations that measure incremental lift rather than headline coverage claims, and make the buy, build, or walk-away call.

  • Specify the licensing, retention, and derivative-use terms the product needs, and treat them as first-class inputs to every sourcing decision rather than an afterthought. Legal, Data Protection, and Data Partnerships paper the deal.

  • Hold the portfolio to its KPIs: decide which sources have earned their cost, which need renegotiating, and which to retire.

Performance measurement and KPIs

  • Define and instrument the KPIs for this product line, including coverage, precision, and recency, and build the internal benchmarking capability to measure them independent of customer-reported feedback.

  • Go a step further than measurement: define the target for each KPI that constitutes winning in the market. This requires competitive benchmarking and direct customer research, and it is the most important judgment call in the role.

  • Quantify the incremental value a subscriber receives per period, and use it to inform pricing and positioning.

  • Use SQL and analytics tooling to interrogate the data yourself rather than waiting on someone else's analysis.

Architecture and platform partnership

  • Partner with platform engineering teams to define how identity signals are resolved, merged across sources, and published, and make the architectural tradeoff calls on where that processing belongs.

  • Shape a generalized, reusable notification mechanism so each new event type is faster to ship than the last.

  • Balance latency, cost, and refresh cadence against the customer value each incremental improvement buys.

Commercialization and go-to-market

  • Define pricing, packaging, and commercial terms for a subscription product, in partnership with Legal, Finance, and Revenue.

  • Identify, recruit, and work hand-in-hand with early-adopter and design-partner customers.

  • Establish and track beta and GA phases, and coordinate cross-functional readiness, including end-to-end testing, to a committed date.

  • Build the positioning, marketing plan, and sales enablement materials with Product Marketing, and be the internal subject matter expert the field relies on.

Customer and competitive research

  • Build a firm, evidence-based read on how we perform against market leaders and where our real differentiation lies.

  • Understand the bar customers will actually accept, and be willing to say which customers and use cases we should not sell to yet.

  • Assess and design around the business risk of getting a high-stakes identity signal wrong.

What you bring

  • Experience: 5+ years in product management, preferably in identity verification, fraud prevention, data products, or other data- and ML-driven products.

  • Data product instinct: Demonstrated experience evaluating, acquiring, and operationalizing acquired data, including designing tests that isolate incremental lift and making the call to walk away when a source doesn't deliver.

  • Technical expertise: Strong understanding of APIs, SQL, databases, event-driven architectures, and product architecture generally.

  • Analytical skills: Comfortable working with data directly, writing queries, and defining measurement methodology, including precision, recall, and coverage benchmarking, to inform product decisions.

  • Commercial judgment on data deals: Has been the product voice in data or technology vendor negotiations; knows what to ask a provider to prove, how licensing, retention, and derivative-use terms constrain what you can build, and when a deal is not worth doing.

  • Commercial ownership: Experience taking a product to market, covering pricing, packaging, beta programs, and launch, not just shipping features.

  • Product judgment: Ability to balance technical complexity, customer needs, regulatory constraints, and business impact, and to set a defensible bar for "good enough to launch" when no precedent exists.

  • Customer focus: Experience working directly with customers, especially in complex or high-stakes environments.

  • Communication: Strong ability to explain complex technical and data concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences, up to and including the executive team.

  • Collaboration: Proven ability to work cross-functionally with Engineering, Data Science, Legal, and go-to-market teams.

Preferred

  • Familiarity with consumer data regulatory frameworks such as GLBA and FCRA, and how they shape product and commercial design.

  • Experience with entity resolution, identity graphs, or record-linkage systems.

  • Experience building a subscription or usage-based data product from zero to first revenue.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Socure’s Partner Ecosystem brings third-party data and decisioning partners into RiskOS. Every partner we onboard has to be integrated cleanly, operated reliably, implemented correctly in customer environments, and understood well enough that our Solutions and Sales teams can put it to work. This role owns the technical side of all of it.

You will be the technical point of accountability for the RiskOS partner ecosystem. You will align with partners on an integration approach. Solutions teams come to you when an implementation doesn't behave. You will define scope, requirements, and priority for the Partner Integration engineering pod. Internal teams come to you to understand what a partner product actually does and when to use it.

This is not just a coordination or ticket-writing role. You will personally run partner API discovery, write the specs the pod builds from, sit in the middle of live troubleshooting, and own the documentation the rest of the company depends on. You will drive the partner engineering pod's roadmap and execution without managing the engineers directly — technical credibility, clarity, and relationships are how the work gets done here.

It is also a role that will grow. As our partner marketplace takes shape, you will be the technical driver behind it: defining what it takes for a partner product to be integrated and consumed at scale.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Own partner integrations end to end

  • Own the program for every new integration: discovery, technical scope, specs, sequencing, and launch readiness — and the pod's roadmap, priorities, and capacity tradeoffs that deliver it.

  • Establish reusable integration patterns — authentication, data mapping, error handling, retries, fallbacks — so each new partner integration is faster than the last.

  • Work with Product and Legal/GRC so contractual and compliance constraints shape the design up front rather than surface as rework.

Be the technical counterpart to our partners

  • Serve as the primary technical contact for partner engineering and solutions teams, from API discovery through release and deprecation cycles.

  • Evaluate partner APIs, data models, SLAs, and support posture to identify the optimal integration path — and push back where their proposed pattern creates fragility, latency, cost, or compliance risk.

  • Define what "integration-ready" means for the marketplace — technical requirements, certification, acceptance criteria — and eventually hold that bar with partners who build into our platform themselves.

Make partner products succeed in customer environments

  • Work with pre-sales Solutions to help them understand partner products: what they do, what they require, what they cost, and what they can't do.

  • Work with post-sales Solutions and Implementation to ensure correct configuration across sandbox and production, and flag workflow designs that will produce poor decisioning outcomes.

  • Build the enablement material that lets Solutions teams handle routine cases independently.

  • Own triage and resolution for integration escalations, define monitoring requirements for integration health, and run a recurring audit cadence that produces remediation rather than a list of known issues.

Own documentation and product expertise — and scale it with AI

  • Own the technical documentation library: integration specs, API references, configuration guides, and troubleshooting runbooks. Treat documentation drift as a defect.

  • Use AI aggressively to draft specs and documentation — with the judgment to catch hallucinated behavior and verify against source API docs — and build repeatable AI patterns so throughput isn't bound by your calendar.

  • Develop working expertise in every partner product and act as the internal explainer for Sales, Solutions, Product, and Support.

WHAT YOU BRING

  • 5+ years in technical program management, technical product management, solutions architecture, solutions engineering, or integration engineering, including direct ownership of external-facing technical work.

  • Demonstrated ability to drive engineering execution without direct authority. You have owned a team's roadmap and delivery as an individual contributor and made it work through influence and credibility.

  • Deep, practical fluency with REST APIs, authentication patterns, webhooks, data mapping and normalization, and the failure modes of third-party dependencies. You can read an API doc set and immediately identify what will break in production.

  • Strong debugging instincts across distributed systems. You are comfortable in logs, traces, and payloads, and can isolate whether a problem is ours, the partner's, or a configuration issue.

  • Proven ability to work directly with external technical teams — holding a firm technical position, saying no well, and keeping the relationship intact.

  • Genuine people skills. This role runs on relationships: with partners, with engineers you don't manage, with Solutions teams under customer pressure, and with leadership. Technical strength alone will not carry it.

  • Exceptional written communication. The specs and documentation you produce are what other teams depend on; writing is a core competency here, not a nice-to-have.

  • Hands-on experience using AI tools in your actual workflow, with the discipline to verify output rather than trust it. You should be able to describe patterns you've built that made recurring work faster for more people than just yourself.

  • Comfort moving between a partner architecture discussion, a customer implementation escalation, and an internal enablement session in the same day.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Background in identity, fraud, risk, KYC/KYB, credit, or adjacent data-provider ecosystems.

  • Experience integrating and operating many third-party data vendors at scale, including managing vendor API versioning and deprecation.

  • Experience building or scaling a partner marketplace, app store, developer platform, or partner certification program.

  • Familiarity with decisioning or workflow orchestration platforms and how data products are composed within them.

  • Experience working alongside pre-sales and post-sales organizations in B2B enterprise SaaS.

  • Exposure to the compliance and contractual dimensions of third-party data use: data rights, permissible purpose, retention, and audit requirements.

  • Prior hands-on engineering background, even if you've since moved into solutions, program, or product work.

The Identity portfolio covers the end-to-end lifecycle of a user and device within the tailnet:

  • Authentication: Integrating with external Identity Providers (IdPs) so users can log in using the credentials they already have (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, etc.).
  • Authorization: Defining how roles, groups, and attributes translate into granular network access policies.
  • Lifecycle Management: Automating the onboarding, offboarding, and synchronization (SCIM) of users and devices as they change roles or leave organizations.

  • Experience shipping products for developer or security-focused audiences: You understand the friction points of modern IAM and know how to build tools that admins and developers actually enjoy using.

About the Role

We are seeking a Product Manager to own Tailscale's networking features — the layer that decides how traffic finds its destination by name on top of Tailscale’s seamless mesh connectivity solution. Concretely, you will own four feature sets: App Connectors, DNS, Funnel, and Tailscale Serve & Services.

A tailnet gives every device an identity and an address. Networking features are what turn addresses into something a person, a script, or an AI agent can actually use — a name, a service, an app, a URL.

  • App Connectors route traffic to specific SaaS and private applications by name, so access follows the app rather than the IP.
  • DNS — MagicDNS, split DNS, custom name servers, search domains
  • Tailscale Serve & Services make a workload — not a machine — the unit of connectivity and access: addressable, load-balanced, and durable across the instances behind it. This is the wedge that lets customers replace a service registry, and eventually much of what they use a service mesh for, with Tailscale.
  • Funnel is Tailscale's ingress story: securely exposing a Service running inside the tailnet to the public internet, from a hobbyist sharing a dev server to production webhooks and public endpoints.

This is the most user-visible role in Tailscale's Dataplane Platform, and the work is as much product design as it is networking. DNS settings, connector topologies, and service definitions are configured by network engineers and IT admins in the admin console, API, and CLI, and the distance between "magical" and "unusable" is the object model, the defaults, and the error messages. 

See How Tailscale Works, Tailscale Funnel, and Four ways to Tailscale a service to learn more.

jobs.description_html:
Thank you for considering Tailscale. If this job description resonates with you, please apply. Frequently cited statistics show that people who identify with historically marginalized groups are likely to apply to jobs only if they meet 100% of the qualifications. We encourage you to help us break that statistic!

About Tailscale 

Tailscale is making safe connection effortless by delivering software that makes it easy to securely interconnect people and their devices, no matter where they are. From hobbyists to multinational corporations, teams of every size use Tailscale each day to protect their networks, share access to internal tools, and more. We're building a future for the Internet that's easy, sensible, and safe, like it used to be. Founded in 2019 and fully distributed, we're backed by Accel, CRV, Insight, Heavybit, and Uncork Capital.

About the Role

Tailscale makes it simple for organizations to securely connect people, devices, and workloads anywhere in the world. As adoption grows within the world’s largest enterprises, we’re launching a Strategic Sales team to support our next stage of growth.

As a founding Strategic Account Executive, you’ll own a focused portfolio of organizations with 10,000+ employees, including Fortune 1000 and Global 2000 companies. You’ll lead complex opportunities from initial engagement through close and expansion, building executive relationships and connecting customer priorities with Tailscale’s capabilities.

You’ll help define how we win in this market - developing outbound strategies, testing new approaches, and creating a playbook for future growth. Reporting to the Director of Strategic Sales, you’ll join a small, highly collaborative team and partner closely with executive leadership and teams across the business.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own account strategy: Build account plans that connect customer priorities with opportunities across business units, geographies, and use cases
  • Create pipeline: Drive personalized outbound prospecting, partnering with SDRs and Marketing on coordinated account-based campaigns
  • Lead complex deals: Manage opportunities through negotiation and close, navigating long sales cycles, competitive pursuits, and complex buying processes
  • Build executive relationships: Earn trust with CIOs, CISOs, CTOs, and senior technical and business leaders while developing champions across the organization
  • Bring the right team together: Partner with Customer Engineering, GTM Engineering, Customer Success, Product, Engineering, executive leadership, Legal, and Finance to win and grow strategic accounts
  • Shape the playbook: Test approaches, share what works, and bring customer feedback to teams shaping Tailscale’s product and enterprise strategy
  • Execute with discipline: Maintain clear qualification, accurate forecasts, and actionable account and opportunity plans

  • 5+ years of success as a top-performing enterprise or strategic seller in early stage, high-growth environments
  • Proven success selling to organizations with 10,000+ employees and closing complex six and seven-figure SaaS deals

  • The ability to earn executive trust, engage technical stakeholders, and navigate procurement, legal, and financial reviews
  • Strong business judgment, clear written and verbal communication, and a collaborative, accountable approach
  • Comfort with ambiguity and enthusiasm for building a sales motion while carrying a quota

jobs.title: Analytics Engineer
jobs.description_html:
We are looking for an Analytics Engineer to join a team dedicated to building the governed data foundation that powers decision-making across Talkiatry. You'll work alongside a collaborative team of engineers to design and maintain reliable, well-documented data models that stakeholders can trust and explore independently.

About Talkiatry:

Talkiatry is transforming mental health care by making high-quality psychiatry more accessible, human, and sustainable for both patients and clinicians. Co-founded by a patient and a triple-board-certified psychiatrist, we were built to solve one of healthcare’s most urgent challenges: millions of people struggle to access mental health care, while clinicians face growing administrative burden and burnout. Through our technology-powered, in-network platform, we’re changing that, creating a better experience for patients and empowering clinicians to focus on delivering exceptional care.

Today, Talkiatry is the largest dedicated psychiatry practice in the U.S., with 750+ psychiatrists, 250+ therapists, and more than two million patient visits delivered nationwide. At our scale, every innovation has real impact. Every workflow we improve, every technology solution we build, and every patient experience we redesign helps thousands of clinicians provide better care to hundreds of thousands of patients. We’re not just growing quickly — we’re redefining how behavioral healthcare is delivered in America.

Joining Talkiatry means joining a mission-driven team that is solving complex problems at scale, driving meaningful change in healthcare, and building the future of mental health care with compassion, innovation, and purpose.

 

You will:

  • Build and maintain clean, scalable, well-documented data models using dbt, Snowflake, and Databricks that serve as the trusted foundation for decision-making across the org

  • Partner with stakeholders to understand business questions and translate them into governed, reusable data products — not one-off reports

  • Contribute to a self-service analytics environment where stakeholders can independently explore data through well-structured, reliable models

  • Adhere to and help evolve our data governance, data quality, and documentation standards

  • Support dashboard and reporting needs where appropriate, with an emphasis on enabling stakeholders rather than building on their behalf

  • Collaborate with data and engineering teams to ensure data products are integrated into the broader product and engineering development process from the start

Your Qualifications:

  • 2 to 3 years of experience in Analytics Engineering, Data Engineering, or a closely related role

  • Proficient SQL skills with a working understanding of data modeling concepts (star schema, slowly changing dimensions, grain)

  • Hands-on experience with dbt and a cloud data warehouse such as Snowflake or BigQuery

  • Familiarity with at least one BI or data exploration tool such as Omni, Looker, or Tableau

  • A bias toward building reusable, documented, and governed data products over ad hoc solutions

  • Exposure to working cross-functionally with non-technical stakeholders to understand business needs

  • Clear communication skills with the ability to explain data concepts and trade-offs to a range of audiences

Why Talkiatry:

  • Top-notch team: we're a diverse, experienced group motivated to make a difference in mental health care

  • Collaborative environment: be part of building something from the ground up at a fast-paced startup

  • Excellent benefits: medical, dental, vision, effective day 1 of employment, 401K with match, generous PTO plus paid holidays, paid parental leave, and more

  • Grow your career with us: hone your skills and build new ones with our Learning team as Talkiatry expands

Talkiatry participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S. only after a job offer is accepted and Form I-9 is completed. For more information on E-Verify, please visit the following: EVerify Participation & IER Right to Work.

At Talkiatry, we are an equal opportunity employer committed to a diverse, inclusive, and equitable workplace and candidate experience. We strive to create an environment where everyone has a sense of belonging and purpose, and where we learn from the unique experiences of those around us.

We encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital or family status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression, pregnancy or caregiver status, veteran status, or any other legally protected status.

  • Establish workflows, troubleshoot barriers, and ensure smooth referral processes

  • Consultative in your approach—you educate, influence, and earn trust

  • Organized, resourceful, and accountable to performance metrics

  • Passionate about improving access to mental health care and helping providers better serve their patients

  • Proven ability to meet or exceed referral or sales growth targets

  • Experience influencing clinicians, administrators, or healthcare stakeholders strongly preferred

  • Comfort working in a fast-growth environment with autonomy and responsibility

  • CRM proficiency (HubSpot or Salesforce preferred)

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Communications, Healthcare Administration, Psychology, or a related field

  • Ability to travel within assigned territory approximately 75% of the time

  • Field autonomy with strong cross-functional support (clinical, operations, marketing)

  • A mission-driven culture focused on expanding access to mental health care

  • A team-first environment rooted in collaboration, knowledge sharing, and shared success

  • Career growth and development, including coaching and a clear advancement path as we scale

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Clinical Operations - Clinical Growth & Success
jobs.description_html:
Talkiatry is growing fast, and the systems that bring new clinicians into the practice have to grow with us. Our Clinical Operations team owns the operating model that helps each clinician move from hire to day-one readiness, build a sustainable caseload, and succeed through the early ramp period.

As Senior Manager, Clinical Operations - Clinical Growth & Success, you'll lead the day-to-day operations and ongoing redesign of that journey. You'll improve how we predict readiness and performance, identify risk early, coordinate targeted interventions, and build repeatable mechanisms that ensure clinicians are successful.

The role connects clinician supply, patient demand, and operational execution. You'll partner across Clinical, Operations, Data, Product, Engineering, Talent Acquisition, and Marketing to remove blockers before they affect a clinician's performance and to recover performance quickly when a clinician falls off track.

This is a hands-on role for an analytical operator who knows how to improve workflows with data, AI, automation, and practical tooling. You do not need to be an engineer. You do need to translate operational problems into clear requirements, build and test lightweight solutions, and work with technical partners when deeper product or data capabilities are required.

  • Experience collaborating closely with product managers and engineers and contributing meaningfully to product strategy, not just execution.

  • Curiosity about emerging technologies and a willingness to learn through experimentation when established design patterns do not yet exist.

  • Experience establishing interaction patterns for emerging technologies where best practices are still being defined.

  • Experience in healthcare or regulated industries.

  • Experience helping establish or significantly evolve the visual language of a product or design system.

  • Experience designing patient-facing or consumer health products.

Genuine enthusiasm for the space, strong foundational product-design skills, and evidence that you can thoughtfully tackle unfamiliar interaction problems matter more than having a particular AI job title on your résumé.

  • Comprehensive benefits: Talkiatry offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with company match, generous paid time off and company holidays, paid parental leave, and additional employee benefits.

jobs.title: Staff Product Manager, Growth
jobs.description_html:
Talkiatry is seeking a Staff Product Manager, Growth to help build our growth engine. You'll initially own our "Start to Visit" funnel, using rigorous analysis, experimentation, and strong product judgment to help more patients successfully begin care.

Growth at Talkiatry has a direct connection to our mission: when we make it easier for someone to discover Talkiatry, find the right clinician, and successfully begin and stay in care, more people get access to the mental health care they need.

You'll identify high-leverage opportunities, develop hypotheses, run rigorous A/B tests, and turn learnings into compounding engines.

Over time, your scope will expand across retention, LTV, organic growth, referrals, and product-led growth loops.

This is a high-impact Staff IC role for an exceptional growth product leader who combines analytical depth, systems thinking, and a relentless drive to learn and optimize.

 

About Talkiatry:

Talkiatry is transforming mental health care by making high-quality psychiatry more accessible, human, and sustainable for both patients and clinicians. Co-founded by a patient and a triple-board-certified psychiatrist, we were built to solve one of healthcare’s most urgent challenges: millions of people struggle to access mental health care, while clinicians face growing administrative burden and burnout. Through our technology-powered, in-network platform, we’re changing that, creating a better experience for patients and empowering clinicians to focus on delivering exceptional care.

 

Today, Talkiatry is the largest dedicated psychiatry practice in the U.S., with 900+ psychiatrists, 400+ therapists, and more than 4 million patient visits delivered nationwide. At our scale, every innovation has real impact. Every workflow we improve, every technology solution we build, and every patient experience we redesign helps thousands of clinicians provide better care to hundreds of thousands of patients. We’re not just growing quickly — we’re redefining how behavioral healthcare is delivered in America.

 

Joining Talkiatry means joining a mission-driven team that is solving complex problems at scale, driving meaningful change in healthcare, and building the future of mental health care with compassion, innovation, and purpose.

 

You will:

  • Own growth product strategy and execution, initially focused on materially improving the Start-to-Visit funnel.

  • Treat growth as a system: deeply understand the funnel, identify constraints and drop-off points, and find the highest-leverage opportunities.

  • Build a rigorous, high-velocity experimentation practice—develop hypotheses, run A/B tests, measure incremental impact, and compound learnings over time.

  • Use funnel analysis, segmentation, cohorts, and behavioral data to understand what is happening and why.

  • Balance continuous optimization with larger product bets that can unlock step-change growth.

  • Expand into retention, LTV, organic acquisition, referrals, and other compounding growth loops over time.

  • Partner deeply across engineering, design, data science, marketing, operations, and clinical teams to drive outcomes.

You have:

  • 7+ years of product management experience, including significant experience building consumer growth products.

  • A track record of materially improving conversion, activation, retention, engagement, or LTV at scale.

  • Exceptional analytical horsepower and fluency with funnels, experimentation, metrics, and behavioral data.

  • Deep expertise in A/B testing, including hypothesis development, experiment design, measurement, and interpretation.

  • Strong systems thinking and an ability to find leverage within complex customer journeys.

  • Exceptional rigor and attention to detail. You interrogate assumptions, dig beneath topline metrics, and care deeply about getting the answer right.

  • Strong product judgment—you know when to optimize, when to keep learning, and when a problem requires a fundamentally different solution.

  • The ability to operate independently in ambiguity and influence cross-functional teams without direct authority.

  • Experience in a world-class consumer growth organization is strongly preferred.

Why Talkiatry:

  • Top-notch team: we're a diverse, experienced group motivated to make a difference in mental health care

  • Collaborative environment: be part of building something from the ground up at a fast-paced startup

  • Excellent benefits: medical, dental, vision, effective day 1 of employment, 401K with match, generous PTO plus paid holidays, paid parental leave, and more!

  • Grow your career with us: hone your skills and build new ones with our Learning team as Talkiatry expands

  • It all comes back to care: we’re a mental health company, and we put our team’s well-being first

jobs.title: Mid-Market Account Executive - NYC based
jobs.description_html:
About Teleport

Don't wait for the future of infrastructure. Be part of it.

Teleport is the AI Infrastructure Identity Company. We're solving one of the hardest problems in security: giving every human, machine, workload, and AI agent a cryptographically secured identity, improving engineering velocity while maintaining security. We make trusted computing simple. This gives you the freedom, power, and autonomy to build and innovate with confidence.

Remote-first and globally distributed, we work with companies like Nasdaq, DoorDash, and Elastic to secure infrastructure for an AI world.

About the Role:

As a Mid-Market Account Executive at Teleport, you will own the full sales cycle for mid-sized organizations looking to secure their infrastructure in an AI-driven world. Teleport unifies identity across humans, machines, workloads, and AI agents — replacing fragmented, credential-based access with a hardware-rooted, cryptographic identity layer that scales zero trust across cloud and on-prem environments. You'll work closely with Sales Engineering, Account Development and Marketing to identify, qualify, and close new business, building a repeatable, high-velocity motion across a defined territory or vertical. This role is ideal for a driven, autonomous seller who thrives on prospecting and closing deals in a fast-paced, high-growth environment — while helping customers eliminate credential sprawl, reduce identity-based attack surface, and prepare their infrastructure for the demands of agentic AI.

What You'll Do:

  • Communicate effectively with Engineering, InfoSec teams, and business stakeholders.

  • Develop a territory plan and relentlessly execute against it in order to exceed your quota.

  • Understand the nuances of selling open source technology.

  • Help us foster our open source community and grow our commercial offering.

  • Identify and excite champions at your key accounts so they become your executive sponsors.

  • Navigate complex deals involving several stakeholders across engineering and InfoSec without coming across as "Salesy."

  • Mentor our Sales Development Reps. You will collaborate with them in order to break into your target accounts.

  • Strong listening and storytelling skills.

What We're Looking For:

  • 3+ years of quota attainment at a software startup in the infrastructure, security, open source space

  • 1+ year experience working at a growing start up selling to scaling AI, fintech or e-commerce companies

  • Experience in articulating the value of a product, aligning with the specific needs and compliance requirements amongst complex organizations

  • Humility, curiosity, resilience, and a sense of humor.

  • You're not afraid of prospecting.

  • Based in NYC

How We Hire — Instructions

Our process is designed to be straightforward and respectful of your time. We skip performative rounds and focus on what matters: understanding how you think and what you can do.

You'll start with a 30-minute recruiter screen, followed by a 30-minute interview with the hiring manager and four team member, a presentation including clear instructions.

Why Teleport

You're joining a company where the problem is real, the team is small, and your work shows up directly in the product. We're not a big company, you won't get lost in a crowd. You'll have the freedom and autonomy to do what you're great at, alongside teammates who care about doing it right and want to see you succeed. The work is collaborative, there's real room to grow, and the mission is one worth showing up for.

Remote-first and globally distributed, we're genuinely passionate about what we're building.

The Benefits

At Teleport, we believe your career is more important than a list of perks. That's why we focus on making your day-to-day the best it can be — giving you the autonomy, access, and support to do the best work of your career.

- Extensive health coverage

- Annual expense budget

- Rest and recovery policies that maximize your ability to recharge

- Investment in your future with retirement savings plans

- Professional development opportunities

Teleport is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate against any employee or applicant on the basis of age, color, disability, gender, national origin, race, religion, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any classifications protected by federal, state, or local law.

jobs.title: Founding Sales Engineer
jobs.description_html:
Founding Sales Engineer (NY, NY or US Remote)

Why we're hiring

Tracebit is helping some of the world's best security teams at Snyk, Docker, Riot Games and many more to achieve an 'assume breach' strategy at scale. Tracebit detects intrusions in critical environments using canaries - decoy assets deployed to deceive attackers.

We're at a massive inflection point and there has never been a more exciting time to join us:

  • We've built a product that security teams love. You'll be our founding Sales Engineer (a key part of our Customer Engineering team), helping build the technical foundation for how we grow our customer base and deliver outcomes at scale.

  • We are backed by some of the best investors in the space (Accel, FirstMark and more).

  • We are growing very quickly (we doubled ARR last quarter), having recently closed some incredible customers that we can't disclose publicly!

  • We are one of the most exciting startups to be part of in cybersecurity, have seen some great feedback from the market and are ready for explosive growth.

  • We have strong traction in the US (80% of our customer base and forward-looking business). We've hit product-market fit and it's time to accelerate our growth by building our US presence.

  • Regularly featured on top startup lists from industry veterans... Creandum's Euro Seed top 50 list, Sifted's 2025 London Startups To Watch, Notions Cloud Top 100, AlbionVC's NHI Breakdown, MMCs Proactive Security Analysis, Accel's Euroscape Top Startups 2024, etc.

  • Trusted by teams at Docker, Chainguard, Xbow, Riot Games, Snyk and more.

  • Our research has recently helped fix a P1 security flaw in Google's Gemini CLI.

Who we're looking for

You have strong technical sales experience. You've spent 3-5 years in a customer-facing technical role at a B2B SaaS company, ideally in cybersecurity or developer tooling. You don't need to code, but you understand and have experience in areas such as cloud infrastructure or DevOps and can explain technical concepts clearly to both engineers and executives.

You learn technical concepts quickly. You can rapidly grasp new technical concepts and translate them into clear value propositions. You're comfortable diving into technical documentation and asking smart questions to fill knowledge gaps.

You work well with GTM teams. You understand the sales process and know when to lead technical discussions versus when to support account executives. You can identify technical blockers and work collaboratively to overcome them.

You're comfortable in startup environments. You've experienced the pace of an early-stage company and this pace excites you. You can handle ambiguity, build processes from scratch, and adapt quickly as priorities shift.

About the role

You'll report directly to Bryan O’Neil, our Director of Customer Engineering. You'll partner closely with sales, product, engineering, and directly with our customers to ensure successful evaluations and wider outcomes via our platform.


Your core focus:

  • Run discovery calls and product demos. Partner with sales to understand prospect requirements and deliver tailored demos that showcase how Tracebit solves their specific challenges. Adjust your approach based on whether you're talking to a CISO or a security engineer.

  • Design and execute PoVs. Scope Proof-of-Values that demonstrate clear alignment within prospect environments. Guide customers through setup, monitor progress, and ensure successful outcomes and technical wins.

  • Build technical sales collateral. Input on demo scripts, technical one-pagers, architecture diagrams, and FAQ documents that help prospects understand our platform. Make it easy for AEs to have informed technical conversations.

  • Provide technical guidance throughout the sales cycle. Address questions about security, compliance, and integrations. Work with engineering when deeper expertise is needed. You will be a Tracebit SME.

  • Feed product insights back to the team. Bring customer feedback, feature requests, and competitive intelligence to product discussions. Help shape what we build based on market needs.

  • Represent Tracebit at events. Attend key cybersecurity conferences to run technical demos, answer questions, and build relationships with prospects.

FAQs

Where is the office?

We're establishing our New York office in Manhattan. You'll work closely with our London team and other US team members as we grow.

Are you doing hybrid/remote?

This role can be based either in our New York office or fully remote in the US. To best support our teams in NY and London, remote locations should be in Eastern or Central US timezones.

We are an office-first company - all of our team works together in the office 5 days a week. However, we're making an exception for this role given the nature of the work and the need to hire the best talent in this space.

If you're based in New York, you'll work from our office. If you're remote, we expect you to come to the office at least quarterly to collaborate with the team in person.

What are the working hours like?

We think 9am-6pm will bring a great cadence to work. As a founding team member, there will definitely be times you need to pick up work outside of these hours, we're keen to limit this where we can but also offer flexibility in return.

Can you sponsor visas?

You must have the right to work in the US.
